translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 278
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 278

sentences.zh: 【後唐紀七】　起玄黓執徐七月，盡閼逢敦牂閏正月，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Later Tang Records 7] From the seventh month of xuanchi jichou through the intercalary first month of yanfeng gengwu, in all a little more than one year.
translations.idiomatic: Later Tang Records 7 — from the seventh month of the year jichou (932) through the intercalary first month of gengwu (933), a little more than one year in all.

sentences.zh: 明宗聖德和武欽孝皇帝下長興三年（

translations.literal: Below: Emperor Mingzong, Sagely Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Reverently Filial — the third year of Changxing (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang — third year of the Changxing era (

sentences.zh: 壬辰，公元九三二年）

translations.literal: renchen, AD 932)
translations.idiomatic: renchen, AD 932)

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛巳，朔方奏夏州党項入寇，擊敗之，追至賀蘭山。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, on xinsi, Shuofang reported that Tangut forces from Xia Prefecture had raided; they were defeated and pursued to Helan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day xinsi, Shuofang reported a Tangut raid from Xia Prefecture; the invaders were defeated and pursued as far as Helan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 己丑，加鎮海、鎮東軍節度使錢元瓘中書令。

translations.literal: On jichou, Qian Yuanguan, military governor of Zhenhai and Zhendong, was given the additional title of Zhongshu Ling.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Qian Yuanguan, governor of the Zhenhai and Zhendong circuits, was also appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，李存瑰至成都，孟知祥拜泣受詔。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Li Cungui arrived at Chengdu; Meng Zhixiang bowed and wept as he received the imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Li Cungui reached Chengdu, where Meng Zhixiang received the edict with bowed head and tears.

sentences.zh: 武安、靜江節度使馬希聲以湖南比年大旱，命閉南嶽及境內諸神祠門，竟不雨。

translations.literal: Ma Xisheng, military governor of Wu'an and Jingjiang, because Hunan had suffered drought for successive years, ordered the gates of Mount Heng and all shrines within the territory closed, yet still no rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xisheng, governor of Wu'an and Jingjiang, had the gates of Mount Heng and every shrine in Hunan closed on account of years of drought — yet still no rain came.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，希聲卒，六軍使袁詮、潘約等迎鎮南節度使希範於朗州而立之。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Xisheng died; the commanders of the Six Armies, Yuan Quan, Pan Yue, and others, went to Lang Prefecture to welcome Ma Xifan, military governor of Zhennan, and installed him.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Xisheng died; Yuan Quan, Pan Yue, and other commanders of the Six Armies fetched Ma Xifan, governor of Zhennan, from Lang Prefecture and enthroned him.

sentences.zh: 乙未，孟知祥遣李存瑰還，上表謝罪，且告福慶公主之喪。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Meng Zhixiang sent Li Cungui back and submitted a memorial asking pardon, also announcing the death of Princess Fuqing.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Meng Zhixiang sent Li Cungui home with a memorial of apology and notice of Princess Fuqing's death.

sentences.zh: 自是復稱籓，然益驕倨矣。

translations.literal: From this time he again styled himself a vassal, yet he became all the more arrogant and haughty.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he again acknowledged vassal status, but grew only more arrogant.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以西京留守、同平章事李從珂為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Li Congke, Western Capital garrison commander and Associate Grand Councilor, was made military governor of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Li Congke, who held the Western Capital and served as Associate Grand Councilor, was appointed military governor of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 廢武興軍，復以鳳、興、文三州隸山南西道。

translations.literal: The Wuxing army was abolished, and the three prefectures of Feng, Xing, and Wen were again placed under Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing garrison was disbanded, and Feng, Xing, and Wen prefectures were restored to Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 丁未，以門下侍郎，同平章事趙鳳同平章事，充安國節度使。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Zhao Feng, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilor, was retained as Associate Grand Councilor and appointed military governor of Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Zhao Feng, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilor, kept his council rank and was sent out as military governor of Anguo.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚申，馬希範至長沙；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on gengshen, Ma Xifan arrived at Changsha;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengshen, Ma Xifan reached Changsha;

sentences.zh: 辛酉，襲位。

translations.literal: on xinyou, he succeeded to the position.
translations.idiomatic: on xinyou he took the throne.

sentences.zh: 甲子，孟知祥令李昊為武泰趙季良等五留後草表，請以知祥為蜀王，行墨制，仍自求旌節，昊曰：「比者諸將攻取方鎮，即有其地，今又自求朝廷節鋮及明公封爵，然則輕重之權皆在群下矣；

translations.literal: On jiazi, Meng Zhixiang had Li Hao draft a memorial for Zhao Jiliang of Wutai and the other five acting military governors, requesting that Zhixiang be made King of Shu with imperial orders issued in ink, while also seeking banners and credentials for himself. Hao said, "Of late the generals have seized a defense command and at once held its territory; now you would also yourself request court commissions and seals of office for my lord — then the weight of authority would all lie with the subordinates;
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Meng Zhixiang ordered Li Hao to draft, on behalf of Zhao Jiliang of Wutai and four other acting governors, a petition to make Zhixiang King of Shu under ink-written edicts, while Zhixiang himself also sought banners and credentials. Hao said, "Lately your generals have taken a circuit and kept it; now you would petition the court for your own commission and title as well — that would put every lever of power in the hands of your subordinates;

sentences.zh: 借使明公自請，豈不可邪！」

translations.literal: even if my lord were to request them himself, would that not also be possible!"
translations.idiomatic: even if you asked for them yourself, would that not serve as well?"

sentences.zh: 知祥大悟，更令昊為己草表，請行墨制，補兩川刺史已下；

translations.literal: Zhixiang was greatly enlightened and had Hao draft a new memorial on his own behalf, requesting ink-written edicts to fill all posts in the Two Rivers from prefect downward;
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang saw the point at once and had Hao draft a new petition in his own name, asking for ink-written appointments to every post in the Two Rivers down to prefect;

sentences.zh: 又表請以季良等五留後為節度使。

translations.literal: he also submitted a memorial asking that Jiliang and the other five acting governors be made full military governors.
translations.idiomatic: and another memorial asking that Jiliang and the other five acting governors receive full governorships.

sentences.zh: 初，安重誨欲圖兩川，自知祥殺李嚴，每除刺史，皆以東兵衛送之，小州不減五百人，夏魯奇、李仁矩、武虔裕各數千人，皆以牙隊為名。

translations.literal: Earlier, An Chonghui had wished to bring the Two Rivers under control; after Zhixiang killed Li Yan, whenever a prefect was appointed, eastern troops were sent as an escort — no small prefecture received fewer than five hundred men; Xia Luqi, Li Renju, and Wu Qianyu each had several thousand, all under the name of "garrison guards."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, An Chonghui had aimed to subdue the Two Rivers; after Zhixiang killed Li Yan, every new prefect was installed with an escort of eastern troops — five hundred at minimum even for a small prefecture, while Xia Luqi, Li Renju, and Wu Qianyu each commanded several thousand men styled "garrison guards."

sentences.zh: 及知祥克遂、閬、利、夔、黔、梓六鎮，得東兵無慮三萬人，恐朝廷征還，表請其妻子。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang had taken the six commands of Sui, Lang, Li, Kui, Qian, and Zi, he obtained nearly thirty thousand eastern troops; fearing the court would recall them, he memorialized asking for their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhixiang had seized the six circuits of Sui, Lang, Li, Kui, Qian, and Zi, he held nearly thirty thousand eastern troops; fearing the court would recall them, he petitioned to have their families sent to join them.

sentences.zh: 吳徐知誥廣金陵城周圍二十里。

translations.literal: In Wu, Xu Zhigao enlarged the city of Jinling to a circumference of twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu, Xu Zhigao expanded Jinling's walls to a circuit of twenty li.

sentences.zh: 初，契丹既強，寇抄盧龍諸州皆遍，幽州城門之外，虜騎充斥。

translations.literal: Earlier, once the Khitans had grown strong, their raids swept every prefecture of Lulong; beyond the gates of You Prefecture, barbarian horsemen filled the land.
translations.idiomatic: After the Khitans grew strong, their raids touched every prefecture of Lulong; beyond Youzhou's gates, enemy horsemen were everywhere.

sentences.zh: 每自涿州運糧入幽州，虜多伏兵於閻溝，掠取之。

translations.literal: Whenever grain was transported from Zhuo Prefecture into You Prefecture, the barbarians often lay ambushes at Yen Gully and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: Grain convoys from Zhuo to Youzhou were repeatedly ambushed at Yen Gully and stripped bare.

sentences.zh: 及趙德鈞為節度使，城閻溝而戍之，為良鄉縣，糧道稍通。

translations.literal: When Zhao Dejun became military governor, he walled Yen Gully and garrisoned it as Liangxiang County; the grain route was gradually opened.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhao Dejun took command, he fortified Yen Gully, garrisoned it as Liangxiang County, and the supply line began to open again.

sentences.zh: 幽州東十里之外，人不敢樵牧；

translations.literal: Within ten li east of You Prefecture, no one dared gather firewood or pasture livestock;
translations.idiomatic: Within ten li east of Youzhou no one dared cut wood or graze herds;

sentences.zh: 德鈞於州東五十里城潞縣而戍之，近州之民始得稼穡。

translations.literal: Dejun walled Lu County fifty li east of the prefecture and garrisoned it; the people near the prefecture were at last able to sow and reap.
translations.idiomatic: Dejun walled and garrisoned Lu County fifty li to the east, and the nearby population could farm again at last.

sentences.zh: 至是，又於州東北百餘里城三河縣以通薊州運路，虜騎來爭，德鈞擊卻之。

translations.literal: At this time he also walled Sanhe County more than a hundred li northeast of the prefecture to open the transport route to Ji Prefecture; barbarian horsemen came to contest it, and Dejun drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Now he walled Sanhe County, more than a hundred li northeast, to secure the route to Jizhou; when Khitan horsemen contested the site, Dejun beat them off.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚辰朔，奏城三河畢。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the first day gengchen, a memorial reported that the walling of Sanhe was complete.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the first day of the month (gengchen), word came that the Sanhe fortification was finished.

sentences.zh: 邊人賴之。

translations.literal: The border people relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier population depended on it.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以鎮南節度使馬希範為武安節度使，兼侍中。

translations.literal: On renwu, Ma Xifan, military governor of Zhennan, was made military governor of Wu'an and also given the title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Ma Xifan was transferred from Zhennan to Wu'an and named Palace Attendant as well.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥命其子仁贊攝行軍司馬，兼都總轄兩川牙內馬步都軍事。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang ordered his son Renzan to act as army marshal and also take overall command of the Two Rivers' palace guard horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang put his son Renzan in charge as acting army marshal and overall commander of the Two Rivers' palace guard forces.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己酉朔，帝復遣李存瓘如成都，凡劍南自節度使、刺史以下官，聽知祥差罷訖奏聞，朝廷更不除人；

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on the first day jiyou, the emperor again sent Li Cunqiong to Chengdu: all offices in Jiannan from military governor and prefect downward were to be appointed and removed by Zhixiang, who would report afterward; the court would appoint no one further;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on the first day of the month (jiyou), the emperor again dispatched Li Cunqiong to Chengdu: every post in Jiannan from governor down would be filled or dismissed by Zhixiang, who need only report afterward — the court would appoint no one else;

sentences.zh: 唯不遣戍兵妻子，然其兵亦不復征也。

translations.literal: only the wives and children of the garrison troops were not sent, yet those troops were also no longer recalled.
translations.idiomatic: only the families of the garrison troops were withheld, but those troops were no longer recalled either.

sentences.zh: 秦王從榮喜為詩，聚浮華之士高輦等於幕府，與相唱和，頗自矜伐。

translations.literal: Prince of Qin Congrong delighted in composing poetry; he gathered flashy talents such as Gao Nian in his staff quarters and exchanged verses with them, greatly prizing himself.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qin Congrong loved to write verse; he gathered flashy literati such as Gao Nian in his staff and traded poems with them, quite pleased with himself.

sentences.zh: 每置酒，輒令僚屬賦詩，有不如意者面毀襲抵棄。

translations.literal: Whenever he set out wine, he would order his subordinates to compose poems; whoever displeased him he would revile to his face, strike, and cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: At every banquet he required his staff to compose poems; anyone who failed to please him was insulted to his face, struck, and cast aside.

sentences.zh: 壬子，從榮入謁，帝語之曰：「吾雖不知書，然喜聞儒生講經義，開益人智思。

translations.literal: On renzi, Congrong came to audience; the emperor said to him, "Though I do not know books, I yet delight to hear Confucian scholars expound the classics — it broadens and benefits men's minds.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Congrong came to court; the emperor told him, "I am no scholar myself, yet I love to hear Confucians lecture on the classics — it widens the mind.

sentences.zh: 吾見莊宗好為詩，將家子文非素習，徒取人竊笑，汝勿效也。」

translations.literal: I saw Zhuangzong fond of poetry — a general's son, letters not his native study, only inviting people's secret laughter. Do not imitate that."
translations.idiomatic: I watched Zhuangzong indulge in poetry — a soldier's son, no training in letters, and people only laughed behind his back. Do not copy him."

sentences.zh: 丙辰，幽州奏契丹屯捺剌泊。

translations.literal: On bingchen, You Prefecture reported that the Khitans were encamped at Nalapo.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Youzhou reported Khitan forces encamped at Nalapo.

sentences.zh: 前影義節度使李金全屢獻馬，上不受，曰：「卿在鎮為治何如？

translations.literal: The former military governor of Yingyi, Li Jinquan, repeatedly presented horses; the emperor would not accept them and said, "How is your governance in your command?
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinquan, former governor of Yingyi, kept sending horses; the emperor refused them and said, "How do you govern your circuit?

sentences.zh: 勿但以獻馬為事！」

translations.literal: Do not make presenting horses your sole business!"
translations.idiomatic: Do not make horse-gifts your whole occupation!"

sentences.zh: 金全，吐谷渾人也。

translations.literal: Jinquan was a man of the Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Jinquan was of Tuyuhun descent.

sentences.zh: 壬申，大理少卿康澄上疏曰：「臣聞童謠非禍福之本，妖祥豈隆替之源！

translations.literal: On renshen, Kang Cheng, Vice Minister of Justice, submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant has heard that children's rhymes are not the root of fortune and misfortune, nor are strange omens the source of a dynasty's rise and fall!
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Kang Cheng, Vice Minister of Justice, memorialized: "I have heard that nursery rhymes are not the root of fortune and ruin, nor are strange omens the source of a dynasty's rise and fall!

sentences.zh: 故雊雉升鼎而桑谷生朝，不能止殷宗之盛；

translations.literal: thus when a crowing pheasant mounted the cauldron and mulberry and grain grew in the court, they could not halt the flourishing of the Yin sovereign;
translations.idiomatic: Yet when a crowing pheasant mounted the cauldron and mulberry and grain sprouted in the court, they did not stop the Yin king's glory;

sentences.zh: 神馬長嘶而玉龜告兆，不能延晉祚之長。

translations.literal: when the divine horse neighed long and the jade tortoise proclaimed a sign, they could not prolong the Jin mandate.
translations.idiomatic: when the divine horse neighed and the jade tortoise foretold disaster, they did not lengthen Jin's reign.

sentences.zh: 是知國家有不足懼者五，有深可畏者六：陰陽不調不足懼，三辰失行不足懼，小人訛言不足懼，山崩川涸不足懼，蟊賊傷稼不足懼；

translations.literal: From this one knows that in a state there are five things not worth fearing and six deeply to be feared: disharmony of yin and yang is not worth fearing; the three luminaries straying from their courses is not worth fearing; base men's false rumors are not worth fearing; mountains collapsing and rivers drying are not worth fearing; locusts harming the crops is not worth fearing;
translations.idiomatic: Thus a state has five things not worth fearing and six that should deeply alarm us: imbalance of yin and yang; the sun, moon, and stars out of course; slander from petty men; mountains collapsing and rivers drying up; locusts ravaging the harvest — none of these need terrify us;

sentences.zh: 賢人藏匿深可畏，四民遷業深可畏，上下相徇深可畏，廉恥道消深可畏，毀譽亂真深可畏，直言蔑聞深可畏。

translations.literal: worthy men in hiding is deeply to be feared; the four classes changing their occupations is deeply to be feared; superiors and inferiors covering for one another is deeply to be feared; the way of integrity and shame being extinguished is deeply to be feared; slander and praise confounding truth is deeply to be feared; forthright speech going unheard is deeply to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: but worthy men in hiding; the four classes abandoning their trades; superiors and inferiors shielding one another; the extinction of shame and integrity; praise and blame confounding truth; honest counsel going unheard — these six should deeply alarm us.

sentences.zh: 不足懼者，願陛下存而勿論；

translations.literal: As to what is not worth fearing, may Your Majesty keep them in mind but not discuss them;
translations.idiomatic: Of the five not worth fearing, may Your Majesty note them but not dwell on them;

sentences.zh: 深可畏者，願陛下修而靡忒。」

translations.literal: as to what is deeply to be feared, may Your Majesty cultivate them and never err."
translations.idiomatic: of the six that should alarm us, may Your Majesty mend them and never stray."

sentences.zh: 優詔獎之。

translations.literal: An edict of special praise rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a commendatory edict in his favor.

sentences.zh: 秦王從榮為人鷹視，輕佻峻急；

translations.literal: Prince of Qin Congrong was hawk-eyed in manner, frivolous, harsh, and impatient;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qin Congrong had a hawk's gaze, was frivolous, harsh, and quick-tempered;

sentences.zh: 既判六軍諸衛事，復參朝政，多驕縱不法。

translations.literal: having been put in charge of the Six Armies and palace guards, he also took part in court government and was often arrogant, unrestrained, and lawless.
translations.idiomatic: once placed over the Six Armies and palace guards he also joined in state affairs, and was often arrogant, unrestrained, and lawless.

sentences.zh: 初，安重誨為樞密使，上專屬任之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when An Chonghui was Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, the emperor entrusted everything to him alone.
translations.idiomatic: When An Chonghui served as Bureau Commissioner, the emperor relied on him exclusively.

sentences.zh: 從榮及宋王從厚自襁褓與之親狎，雖典兵，常為重誨所制，畏事之。

translations.literal: Congrong and Prince of Song Conghou had been intimate with him from infancy; though they commanded troops, they were often restrained by Chonghui and feared to cross him.
translations.idiomatic: Congrong and Prince of Song Conghou had known him since infancy; though they held armies, Chonghui still kept them in check and they feared him.

sentences.zh: 重誨死，王淑妃與宣徽使孟漢瓊宣傳帝命，范延光、趙延壽為樞密使，從榮皆輕侮之。

translations.literal: After Chonghui died, Consort Wang Shufei and the Palace Service Commissioner Meng Hanqiong proclaimed the emperor's orders; Fan Yanguang and Zhao Shou were made Bureau Commissioners — Congrong treated them all with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: After Chonghui's death, Consort Wang Shufei and Palace Service Commissioner Meng Hanqiong relayed the emperor's orders; Fan Yanguang and Zhao Shou became Bureau Commissioners — Congrong despised them all.

sentences.zh: 河陽節度使、同平章事石敬瑭兼六軍諸衛副使，其妻永寧公主與從榮異母，素相憎疾。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang, military governor of Heyang and Associate Grand Councilor, also served as deputy commander of the Six Armies and palace guards; his wife Princess Yongning was a half-sister of Congrong by a different mother, and they had long hated each other.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang, governor of Heyang and Associate Grand Councilor, also served as deputy commander of the Six Armies and palace guards; his wife Princess Yongning, Congrong's half-sister by another mother, had long detested him.

sentences.zh: 從榮以從厚聲名出己右，尤忌之；

translations.literal: Congrong, because Conghou's reputation stood above his own, especially resented him;
translations.idiomatic: Congrong especially resented Conghou, whose reputation outshone his own;

sentences.zh: 從厚善以卑弱奉之，故嫌隙不外見。

translations.literal: Conghou was skilled at serving him with humility and weakness, so their enmity did not show outwardly.
translations.idiomatic: Conghou knew how to court him with humility, so their rift never showed openly.

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭不欲與從榮共事，常思外補以避之。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang did not wish to serve alongside Congrong and often thought of an outside appointment to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang wanted no part of serving beside Congrong and kept looking for a provincial post to escape him.

sentences.zh: 范延光、趙延壽亦慮及禍，屢辭機要，請與舊臣迭為之，上不許。

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang and Zhao Shou also feared disaster, repeatedly resigned the key posts, and asked to rotate the duty with older ministers — the emperor would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang and Zhao Shou likewise feared for their lives, repeatedly tried to quit the Bureau, and asked to rotate the post among senior ministers — the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 會契丹欲入寇，上命擇帥臣鎮河東，延光、延壽皆曰：「當今帥臣可往者，獨石敬瑭、康義誠耳。」

translations.literal: When the Khitans were about to invade, the emperor ordered a commander chosen to secure Hedong; Yanguang and Shou both said, "Of commanders fit to go today, only Shi Jingtang and Kang Yicheng will do."
translations.idiomatic: As the Khitans prepared to invade, the emperor ordered a commander for Hedong; Yanguang and Shou both said, "Among today's commanders, only Shi Jingtang and Kang Yicheng are fit to go."

sentences.zh: 敬瑭亦願行，上即命除之。

translations.literal: Jingtang also wished to go, and the emperor at once appointed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang was willing to go, and the emperor appointed him at once.

sentences.zh: 既受詔，不落六軍副使，敬瑭復辭，上乃以宣徽使朱弘昭知山南東道，代義誠詣闕。

translations.literal: After receiving the edict he did not relinquish the deputy command of the Six Armies; Jingtang declined again, and the emperor then had the Palace Service Commissioner Zhu Hongzhao take charge of Shannan East Circuit to replace Yicheng and come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had the edict he still would not give up his deputy command; Jingtang declined again, so the emperor sent Palace Service Commissioner Zhu Hongzhao to hold Shannan East in Yicheng's place and summon Yicheng to court.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛巳，以三司使孟秸為忠武節度使，以忠武節度使馮贇充宣徽南院使，判三司。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinsi, Meng Jie, Commissioner of the Three Departments, was made military governor of Zhongwu; Feng Yun, military governor of Zhongwu, was made Commissioner of the Southern Palace Service Bureau and also directed the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on xinsi, Three Departments Commissioner Meng Jie was appointed governor of Zhongwu; Zhongwu governor Feng Yun became Southern Palace Service Commissioner and continued to head the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 鵠本刀筆吏，與范延光鄉里厚善，數年間引擢至節度使；

translations.literal: Feng Yun had originally been a clerical officer; he was on close terms with Fan Yanguang as a fellow townsman, and within a few years was promoted all the way to military governor;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yun had begun as a clerk; a fellow townsman of Fan Yanguang, he was raised within a few years to a governorship;

sentences.zh: 上雖知其太速，然不能違也。

translations.literal: the emperor, though he knew the pace was too swift, could not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor knew the promotion was too fast but could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，上以胡寇浸逼北邊，命趣議河東帥；

translations.literal: On yiyou, because barbarian raiders were pressing the northern border, the emperor ordered a swift council on the Hedong commander;
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, with barbarian raids pressing the north, the emperor ordered an urgent council on who should command Hedong;

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭欲之，而范延光、趙延壽欲用康義誠，議久不決。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang wanted the post, but Fan Yanguang and Zhao Shou wished to use Kang Yicheng; deliberation dragged on without decision.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang wanted the post, but Fan Yanguang and Zhao Shou favored Kang Yicheng, and debate dragged on.

sentences.zh: 樞密直學士李崧以為非石太尉不可。

translations.literal: Li Song, Academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, held that none but Vice Marshal Shi would do.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau Academician Li Song insisted that only Vice Marshal Shi would do.

sentences.zh: 延光曰：「僕亦累奏用之，上欲留之宿衛耳。」

translations.literal: Yanguang said, "I too have repeatedly memorialized to use him; the emperor only wishes to keep him in the palace guard."
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang said, "I have memorialized for him repeatedly; the emperor only wants to keep him on palace guard duty."

sentences.zh: 會上遣中使趣之，眾乃從崧議。

translations.literal: Just then the emperor sent a palace envoy to hurry them, and the assembly followed Song's view.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the emperor sent an envoy to hurry them along, and the court fell in with Song's view.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以石敬瑭為北京留守、河東節度使，兼大同、振武、彰國、威塞等軍蕃漢馬步總管，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Shi Jingtang was made garrison commander of the Northern Capital and military governor of Hedong, and also overall commander of the barbarian and Han horse and foot forces of Datong, Zhenwu, Zhangguo, Weisai, and other armies, with the additional title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Shi Jingtang was named Northern Capital garrison commander and Hedong governor, overall commander of the barbarian and Han forces of Datong, Zhenwu, Zhangguo, Weisai, and related armies, and also Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 己丑，加樞密使趙延壽同平章事。

translations.literal: On jichou, Bureau Commissioner Zhao Shou was given the additional title of Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Bureau Commissioner Zhao Shou was also named Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 吳以諸道都統徐知誥為大丞相、太師，加領德勝節度使；

translations.literal: Wu made Xu Zhigao, Overall Commander of All Circuits, Grand Chancellor and Grand Preceptor, and also gave him charge of the Desheng command;
translations.idiomatic: Wu made Overall Commander Xu Zhigao Grand Chancellor and Grand Preceptor, and also gave him the Desheng command;

sentences.zh: 知誥矢丞相、太師。

translations.literal: Zhigao declined the posts of Chancellor and Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao declined Chancellor and Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 大同節度使張敬達聚兵要害，契丹竟不敢南下而還。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingda, military governor of Datong, massed troops at a strategic point; the Khitans at last dared not push south and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Datong governor Zhang Jingda massed troops at a choke point; the Khitans at last dared not advance south and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 敬達，代州人也。

translations.literal: Jingda was a man of Dai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jingda was from Dai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蔚州刺史張彥超本沙陀人，嘗為帝養子，與石敬瑭有隙；

translations.literal: Zhang Yanchao, prefect of Wei Prefecture, was originally a Shatuo; he had once been the emperor's adopted son and bore a grudge against Shi Jingtang;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Prefecture governor Zhang Yanchao was a Shatuo who had once been the emperor's adopted son and bore a grudge against Shi Jingtang;

sentences.zh: 聞敬瑭為總管，舉城附於契丹，契丹以為大同節度使。

translations.literal: hearing that Jingtang had become overall commander, he surrendered his city to the Khitans, who made him military governor of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: when he heard Jingtang had become overall commander, he surrendered his city to the Khitans, who named him governor of Datong.

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭至晉陽，以部將劉知遠、周瑰為都押衙，委以心腹；

translations.literal: When Shi Jingtang reached Jinyang, he made his subordinate generals Liu Zhiyuan and Zhou Gui chief military administrators and entrusted them as his intimates;
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Jingtang reached Jinyang, he made subordinates Liu Zhiyuan and Zhou Gui chief military administrators and trusted them as his inner circle;

sentences.zh: 軍事委知遠，帑藏委瑰。

translations.literal: military affairs he entrusted to Zhiyuan, the treasury to Gui.
translations.idiomatic: military affairs to Zhiyuan, the treasury to Gui.

sentences.zh: 瑰，晉陽人也。

translations.literal: Gui was a man of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was a native of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊午，以康義誠為河陽節度使，兼侍衛親軍馬步都指揮使；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuwu, Kang Yicheng was made military governor of Heyang and also Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard horse and foot;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuwu, Kang Yicheng was appointed governor of Heyang and Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard horse and foot;

sentences.zh: 以朱弘昭為山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: Zhu Hongzhao was made military governor of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongzhao was made governor of Shannan East.

sentences.zh: 是歲，漢主立其子耀樞為雍正，龜圖為康王，弘度為賓王，弘熙為晉王，弘昌為越王，弘弼為齊王，弘雅為韶王，弘澤為鎮王，弘操為萬王，弘杲為循王，弘暐為思王，弘邈為高王，弘簡為同王，弘建為益王，弘濟為辯王，弘道為貴王，弘昭為宜王，弘政為通王，弘益為定王；

translations.literal: That year the ruler of Han enfeoffed his sons: Yaoshu as Prince of Yong, Guitu as Prince of Kang, Hongdu as Prince of Bin, Hongxi as Prince of Jin, Hongchang as Prince of Yue, Hongbi as Prince of Qi, Hongya as Prince of Shao, Hongze as Prince of Zhen, Hongcao as Prince of Wan, Honggao as Prince of Xun, Hongwei as Prince of Si, Hongmiao as Prince of Gao, Hongjian as Prince of Tong, Hongjian as Prince of Yi, Hongji as Prince of Bian, Hongdao as Prince of Gui, Hongzhao as Prince of Yi, Hongzheng as Prince of Tong, and Hongyi as Prince of Ding;
translations.idiomatic: That year the Han ruler enfeoffed his sons: Yaoshu as Prince of Yong, Guitu as Prince of Kang, Hongdu as Prince of Bin, Hongxi as Prince of Jin, Hongchang as Prince of Yue, Hongbi as Prince of Qi, Hongya as Prince of Shao, Hongze as Prince of Zhen, Hongcao as Prince of Wan, Honggao as Prince of Xun, Hongwei as Prince of Si, Hongmiao as Prince of Gao, Hongjian as Prince of Tong, Hongjian as Prince of Yi, Hongji as Prince of Bian, Hongdao as Prince of Gui, Hongzhao as Prince of Yi, Hongzheng as Prince of Tong, and Hongyi as Prince of Ding;

sentences.zh: 未幾，徙弘度為秦王。

translations.literal: Before long Hongdu was transferred to Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Hongdu was made Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 明宗聖德和武欽孝皇帝下長興四年（

translations.literal: Below: Emperor Mingzong, Sagely Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Reverently Filial — the fourth year of Changxing (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang — fourth year of the Changxing era (

sentences.zh: 癸巳，公元九三三年）

translations.literal: guisi, AD 933)
translations.idiomatic: guisi, AD 933)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊子，加秦王從榮守尚書令，兼侍中。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on wuzi, Prince of Qin Congrong was given charge of the Directorate of the Secretariat and also made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on wuzi, Prince of Qin Congrong was named Director of the Secretariat and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以端明殿學士歸義劉昫為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Liu Xu of Guiyi, Academician of the Hall of Duanming, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Liu Xu of Guiyi, a Duanming Hall academician, was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 閩人有言真封宅龍見者，閩王延鈞更命其宅曰龍躍宮。

translations.literal: A man of Min reported that a dragon had appeared at the Zhenfeng residence; Prince of Min Yanjun renamed the residence Dragon Leap Palace.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Min reported a dragon at the Zhenfeng residence; Prince of Min Yanjun renamed it Dragon Leap Palace.

sentences.zh: 遂詣寶皇宮受冊，備儀衛，入府，即皇帝位，國號大閩，大赦，改元龍啟；

translations.literal: He then went to the Baohuang Palace to receive the investiture, with full ceremonial guard, entered his residence, and took the imperial throne; the state was named Great Min, a general amnesty was proclaimed, and the era name was changed to Longqi;
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Baohuang Palace for investiture with full ceremonial guard, entered his residence, and took the throne; the state was named Great Min, a general amnesty was proclaimed, and the era was renamed Longqi;

sentences.zh: 更名璘。

translations.literal: He changed his name to Lin.
translations.idiomatic: He took the name Lin.

sentences.zh: 追尊父祖，立五廟。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored his father and forefathers and established five ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored his father and ancestors and established five ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 以其僚屬李敏為左僕射、門下侍郎，其子節度副使繼鵬為右僕射、中書侍郎，並同平章事；

translations.literal: He made his staff member Li Min Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and Vice Director of the Chancellery, and his son Jipeng, deputy military governor, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and Vice Director of the Secretariat — both as Associate Grand Councilors;
translations.idiomatic: He made staff member Li Min Left Vice Director and Vice Director of the Chancellery, and his son Jipeng, deputy governor, Right Vice Director and Vice Director of the Secretariat — both as Associate Grand Councilors;

sentences.zh: 以親吏吳勖為樞密使。

translations.literal: he made his personal clerk Wu Xu Bureau Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: he made personal clerk Wu Xu Bureau Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 唐冊禮使裴傑、程侃適至海門，閩主以傑為如京使；

translations.literal: Tang envoys for investiture rites, Pei Jie and Cheng Kan, happened to reach Haimen; the ruler of Min made Jie envoy to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Tang investiture envoys Pei Jie and Cheng Kan happened to reach Haimen; the Min ruler made Jie envoy to the Tang capital;

sentences.zh: 侃固求北還，不許。

translations.literal: Kan urgently asked to return north, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Kan pleaded to return north, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 閩主自以國小地僻，常謹事四鄰，由是境內差安。

translations.literal: The ruler of Min, because his state was small and the land remote, always dealt carefully with the four neighboring states; by this the territory within the borders was comparatively at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Because his realm was small and remote, the Min ruler always treated his neighbors with care, and the country enjoyed a measure of calm.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊申，孟知祥墨制以趙季良等為五鎮節度使。

translations.literal: In the second month, on wushen, Meng Zhixiang issued ink-written orders making Zhao Jiliang and the others military governors of the five commands.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wushen, Meng Zhixiang used ink-written orders to appoint Zhao Jiliang and the others governors of five circuits.

sentences.zh: 涼州大將拓跋承謙及耆老上表，請以權知留後孫超為節度使。

translations.literal: The great general of Liang Prefecture, Tuo Ba Chengqian, and the elders submitted a memorial asking that Sun Chao, acting military governor, be made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Prefecture general Tuoba Chengqian and local elders petitioned to make acting governor Sun Chao full military governor.

sentences.zh: 上問使者：「超為何人？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the envoy, "Who is Chao?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the envoy, "Who is Chao?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「張義潮在河西，朝廷以天平軍二千五百人戍涼州。

translations.literal: He answered, "When Zhang Yichao held Hexi, the court garrisoned Liang Prefecture with twenty-five hundred men of the Tianping army.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "When Zhang Yichao held Hexi, the court posted twenty-five hundred Tianping troops to garrison Liang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自黃巢之亂，涼州為党項所隔，鄆人稍稍物故皆盡，超及城中之人皆其子孫也。」

translations.literal: Since the disorders of Huang Chao, Liang Prefecture has been cut off by the Tanguts; the men of Yan gradually died off until none remained, and Chao and the people in the city are all their descendants."
translations.idiomatic: Since Huang Chao's rebellion, Liang Prefecture has been cut off by the Tanguts; the Yan men posted there died off one by one until none were left, and Chao and everyone in the city are their descendants."

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以馬希範為武安、武平節度使，兼中書令。

translations.literal: On yimao, Ma Xifan was made military governor of Wu'an and Wuping and also given the title of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Ma Xifan was appointed governor of Wu'an and Wuping and also named Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 戊午，定難節度使李仁福卒；

translations.literal: On wuwu, Li Renfu, military governor of Dingnan, died;
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Dingnan governor Li Renfu died;

sentences.zh: 庚申，軍中立其子彝超為留後。

translations.literal: on gengshen the army installed his son Yichao as acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: on gengshen the army installed his son Yichao as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以孟知祥為東西川節度使、蜀王。

translations.literal: On guihai, Meng Zhixiang was made military governor of the Eastern and Western Sichuan circuits and King of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Meng Zhixiang was named governor of Eastern and Western Sichuan and King of Shu.

sentences.zh: 先是，河西諸鎮皆言李仁福潛通契丹，朝廷恐其與契丹連兵，併吞河右，南侵關中，會仁福卒，三月，癸未，以其子彝超為彰武留後，徙彰武節度使安從進為定難留後，仍命靜難節度使藥彥稠將兵五萬，以宮苑使安重益為監軍，送從進赴鎮。

translations.literal: Earlier, all the commands west of the Yellow River had reported that Li Renfu was in secret contact with the Khitans; the court feared he would join forces with them, swallow the lands west of the river, and invade south into Guanzhong. When Renfu died, in the third month, on guiwei, his son Yichao was made acting military governor of Zhangwu; An Congjin, military governor of Zhangwu, was transferred to acting military governor of Dingnan; and Yao Yanchou, military governor of Jingnan, was ordered to lead fifty thousand troops, with the Palace Parks Commissioner An Chongyi as army supervisor, to escort Congjin to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, every command west of the Yellow River had reported that Li Renfu was secretly dealing with the Khitans; the court feared a joint campaign that would swallow the west and strike south into Guanzhong. When Renfu died, in the third month, on guiwei, his son Yichao was made acting governor of Zhangwu; Zhangwu governor An Congjin was shifted to acting governor of Dingnan; and Jingnan governor Yao Yanchou was ordered to lead fifty thousand men, with Palace Parks Commissioner An Chongyi as supervisor, to escort Congjin to his post.

sentences.zh: 從進，索葛人也。

translations.literal: Congjin was a man of the Suoge.
translations.idiomatic: Congjin was a Suoge tribesman.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，始下制除趙季良等為五鎮節度使。

translations.literal: On yiyou, formal edicts were at last issued appointing Zhao Jiliang and the others military governors of the five commands.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, formal edicts at last appointed Zhao Jiliang and the others governors of five circuits.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，敕諭夏、銀、綏、宥將士吏民，以「夏州窮邊，李彝超年少，未能扞御，故徙之延安，從命則有李從曮、高允韜富貴之福，違命則有王都、李匡賓覆族之禍。」

translations.literal: On dinghai, an edict addressed the officers, soldiers, clerks, and people of Xia, Yin, Sui, and You, saying, "Xia Prefecture is a poor frontier; Li Yichao is young and unable to defend it, and therefore he is being moved to Yan'an. Obey the order and you will have the wealth and honor of Li Congyan and Gao Yuntao; defy it and you will have the clan-destroying disaster of Wang Du and Li Kuangbin."
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, an edict addressed the troops and people of Xia, Yin, Sui, and You: "Xia Prefecture is a poor frontier post; Li Yichao is young and cannot hold it, so he is being moved to Yan'an. Obey and you share the rewards of Li Congyan and Gao Yuntao; resist and you share the ruin of Wang Du and Li Kuangbin."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，彝超上言，為軍士百姓擁留，未得赴鎮，詔遣使趣之。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, Yichao memorialized that soldiers and commoners had detained him and he could not proceed to his post; an edict sent envoys to hurry him on.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Yichao reported that troops and civilians had detained him and he could not take up his post; the court sent envoys to hurry him along.

sentences.zh: 言事者請為親王置師傅，宰相畏秦王從榮，不敢除人，請令王自擇。

translations.literal: Memorialists asked that tutors be appointed for the imperial princes; the chief ministers feared Prince of Qin Congrong and dared not appoint anyone, and asked that the prince choose for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists asked that tutors be appointed for the imperial princes; the chief ministers feared Prince of Qin Congrong and dared not choose anyone themselves, and asked the prince to choose.

sentences.zh: 秦王府判官、太子詹事王居敏薦兵部侍郎劉瓚於從榮，從榮表請之。

translations.literal: Wang Jumin, administrative aide to the Prince of Qin and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, recommended to Congrong the Vice Minister of War Liu Zan; Congrong memorialized requesting him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jumin, an aide on the Prince of Qin's staff and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, recommended Vice Minister of War Liu Zan to Congrong, who memorialized for his appointment.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以瓚為秘書監、秦王傅，前襄州支使山陽魚崇遠為記室。

translations.literal: On guichou, Zan was made Director of the Secretariat and tutor to the Prince of Qin; Yu Chongyuan of Shanyang, former aide of Xiang Prefecture, was made recorder.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Zan was named Director of the Secretariat and tutor to the Prince of Qin; Yu Chongyuan of Shanyang, formerly an aide at Xiang Prefecture, was made recorder.

sentences.zh: 瓚自以左遷，泣訴，不得免。

translations.literal: Zan regarded himself as demoted, wept and pleaded, but could not be excused.
translations.idiomatic: Zan took the post as a demotion, wept and pleaded to be released, but could not escape it.

sentences.zh: 王府參佐皆新進少年，輕脫諂諛，瓚獨從容規諷，從榮不悅。

translations.literal: The prince's staff were all newly risen young men, frivolous and flattering; Zan alone calmly admonished him, and Congrong was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's staff were all newly risen young men, frivolous and sycophantic; only Zan calmly admonished him, and Congrong disliked it.

sentences.zh: 瓚雖為傅，從榮一概以僚屬待之，瓚有難色；

translations.literal: though Zan was his tutor, Congrong treated him altogether as a staff member; Zan showed distress;
translations.idiomatic: Though Zan was his tutor, Congrong treated him like any other staff member; Zan looked pained;

sentences.zh: 從榮覺之，自是戒門者勿為通，月聽一至府，或竟日不召，亦不得食。

translations.literal: Congrong noticed this and from then on ordered the gatekeepers not to admit him; once a month he was allowed one visit to the residence, or sometimes he was not summoned all day and was given no food.
translations.idiomatic: Congrong noticed and thereafter told the gatekeepers not to admit him; once a month he might be allowed one visit, or sometimes he was not summoned all day and went without food.

sentences.zh: 李彝超不奉詔，遣共兄阿囉王守青嶺門，集境內党項諸胡以自救。

translations.literal: Li Yichao did not obey the edict; he sent his elder brother Aluo to hold Qingling Pass and gathered the Tanguts and various barbarians within his territory to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yichao refused the edict; he sent his elder brother Aluo to hold Qingling Pass and rallied the Tanguts and other tribes within his territory to defend himself.

sentences.zh: 藥彥稠等進屯蘆關，彝超遣党項抄糧運及攻具，官軍自蘆關退保金明。

translations.literal: Yao Yanchou and the others advanced and encamped at Luguan; Yichao sent Tanguts to raid grain convoys and siege equipment, and the government army withdrew from Luguan to hold Jinming.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yanchou and the others advanced to Luguan; Yichao sent Tanguts to raid grain convoys and siege gear, and the government army fell back from Luguan to Jinming.

sentences.zh: 閩王璘立子繼鵬為福王，充寶皇宮使。

translations.literal: The King of Min, Lin, made his son Jipeng Prince of Fu and appointed him commissioner of the Baohuang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: King of Min Lin made his son Jipeng Prince of Fu and put him in charge of the Baohuang Palace.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊寅，立皇子從珂為潞王，從益為許王，從子天平節度使從溫為兗王，護國節度使從璋為洋王，成德節度使從敏為涇王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on wuyin, the imperial sons were enfeoffed: Congke as Prince of Lu, Congyi as Prince of Xu, the emperor's nephew Congwen, military governor of Tianping, as Prince of Yan, Congzhang of Huguo as Prince of Yang, and Congmin of Chengde as Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on wuyin, imperial sons were enfeoffed: Congke as Prince of Lu, Congyi as Prince of Xu, the emperor's nephew and Tianping governor Congwen as Prince of Yan, Huguo governor Congzhang as Prince of Yang, and Chengde governor Congmin as Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，閩地震，閩主璘避位修道，命福王繼鵬權總萬機。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Min was shaken by an earthquake; the ruler of Min, Lin, yielded the throne to cultivate the Way and ordered Prince of Fu Jipeng to handle state affairs provisionally.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, an earthquake struck Min; King Lin yielded the throne to pursue religious cultivation and put Prince of Fu Jipeng in charge of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，閩王審知性節儉，府捨皆庳陋；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Prince of Min Shen Zhixing was in power, he was frugal by nature and the government buildings were all low and plain;
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Min Shen Zhixing ruled, he was frugal by nature and government buildings were modest;

sentences.zh: 至是，大作宮殿，極土木之盛。

translations.literal: at this time he undertook great palace construction, carrying earth and wood works to the utmost splendor.
translations.idiomatic: now he undertook vast palace construction, lavishing every extravagance of timber and stone.

sentences.zh: 甲申，帝暴得風疾；

translations.literal: On jiashen, the emperor suddenly suffered a wind stroke;
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the emperor was suddenly stricken with apoplexy;

sentences.zh: 庚寅，小愈，見群臣於文明殿。

translations.literal: on gengyin he recovered somewhat and received the ministers in the Hall of Civilization.
translations.idiomatic: on gengyin he improved slightly and received the ministers in the Hall of Civilization.

sentences.zh: 壬辰夜，夏州城上舉火，比明，雜虜數千騎救之，安從進遣先鋒使宋溫擊走之。

translations.literal: On the night of renchen, signal fires were raised atop the walls of Xia Prefecture; by dawn several thousand mixed barbarian horsemen came to its relief, and An Congjin sent his vanguard commander Song Wen to drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of renchen, signal fires blazed on the walls of Xia Prefecture; by dawn several thousand barbarian horsemen came to relieve it, and An Congjin sent vanguard commander Song Wen to drive them off.

sentences.zh: 吳宋齊丘勸徐知誥徙吳主都金陵，知誥乃營宮城於金陵。

translations.literal: Song Qiqiu of Wu urged Xu Zhigao to move the Wu ruler's capital to Jinling; Zhigao then built a palace city at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu of Wu urged Xu Zhigao to move the Wu capital to Jinling; Zhigao then built a palace city there.

sentences.zh: 帝旬日不見群臣，都人忷懼，或潛竄山野，或寓止軍營。

translations.literal: For ten days the emperor did not see the ministers; the people of the capital were agitated with fear, some secretly fleeing into mountains and wilds, others lodging in military camps.
translations.idiomatic: For ten days the emperor did not appear before the ministers; the capital was gripped with fear, some people hiding in the hills, others taking shelter in army camps.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庚辰，帝力疾御廣壽殿，人情始安。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, on gengchen, the emperor, straining against his illness, held court in the Hall of Broad Longevity, and popular feeling at last grew calm.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on gengchen, the emperor, forcing himself despite his illness, held court in the Hall of Broad Longevity, and the capital at last settled.

sentences.zh: 安從進攻夏州。

translations.literal: An Congjin attacked Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An Congjin besieged Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州城赫連勃勃所築，堅如鐵石，斫鑿不能入。

translations.literal: The prefectural city had been built by Helian Bobo; it was hard as iron and stone, and neither chopping nor boring could penetrate it.
translations.idiomatic: The city had been built by Helian Bobo; its walls were hard as iron and stone, and neither axe nor drill could breach them.

sentences.zh: 又党項萬餘騎徜徉四野，抄掠糧餉，官軍無所芻牧。

translations.literal: Moreover more than ten thousand Tangut horsemen roamed the four quarters of the countryside, raiding grain and fodder, so the government army had nowhere to gather forage.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand Tangut horsemen also ranged the countryside, raiding grain and fodder, so the government army could find no pasture or forage.

sentences.zh: 山路險狹，關中民輸斗粟束蒿費錢數緡，民間困竭不能供。

translations.literal: The mountain roads were narrow and perilous; for the people of Guanzhong to deliver a dou of grain or a bundle of hay cost several strings of cash, and the populace was exhausted and unable to supply it.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain roads were narrow and dangerous; delivering a single dou of grain or bundle of hay from Guanzhong cost several strings of cash, and the people were exhausted and could not keep up.

sentences.zh: 李彝超兄弟登城謂從進曰：「夏州貧瘠，非有珍寶蓄積可以充朝廷貢賦也；

translations.literal: Li Yichao and his brothers mounted the wall and said to Congjin, "Xia Prefecture is poor and barren; it has no stored treasures or riches that could meet the court's tribute and taxes;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yichao and his brothers mounted the wall and called to Congjin, "Xia Prefecture is poor and barren; it holds no hoard of treasure that could pay the court's tribute;

sentences.zh: 但以祖父世守此土，不欲失之。

translations.literal: it is only that our forefathers have held this land for generations, and we do not wish to lose it.
translations.idiomatic: our forefathers have held this land for generations, and we do not wish to lose it.

sentences.zh: 蕞爾孤城，勝之不武，何足煩國家勞費如此！

translations.literal: This tiny lone city — to conquer it would be unworthy of martial honor; why should the state trouble itself with such labor and expense!
translations.idiomatic: This tiny lone city — to take it would be unworthy; why should the state spend so much labor and treasure on it!

sentences.zh: 幸為表聞，若許其自新，或使之征伐，願為眾先。」

translations.literal: We beg you to memorialize on our behalf; if we are allowed to reform, or if we are sent on campaign, we are willing to lead the host."
translations.idiomatic: Please report this for us; if we are allowed to reform, or if we are sent on campaign, we will lead the host."

sentences.zh: 上聞之，壬午，命從進引兵還。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this, on renwu he ordered Congjin to withdraw his troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, on renwu he ordered Congjin to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 其後有知李仁福陰事者，云：「仁福畏朝廷除移，揚言結契丹為援，契丹實不與之通也；

translations.literal: Later someone who knew Li Renfu's private affairs said, "Renfu feared removal by the court and spread word that he was joining the Khitans for aid, but the Khitans in fact had no dealings with him;
translations.idiomatic: Later someone who knew Li Renfu's private dealings said, "Renfu feared removal by the court and spread word that he was allying with the Khitans, but the Khitans in fact had no contact with him;

sentences.zh: 致朝廷誤興是役，無功而還。」

translations.literal: this led the court mistakenly to launch this campaign and return without success."
translations.idiomatic: this led the court mistakenly to launch this campaign and return empty-handed."

sentences.zh: 自是夏州輕朝廷，每有叛臣，必陰與之連以邀賂遺。

translations.literal: From this time Xia Prefecture held the court in light esteem; whenever there was a rebel minister, it would secretly join with him to seek bribes and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Xia Prefecture held the court in contempt; whenever a rebel appeared, it would secretly ally with him to extract bribes.

sentences.zh: 上疾久未平，征夏州無功，軍士頗有流言，乙酉，賜在京諸軍優給有差；

translations.literal: The emperor's illness had long not abated; the campaign against Xia Prefecture had achieved nothing, and among the soldiers there was much loose talk; on yiyou he granted graded special payments to all armies in the capital;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's illness lingered; the Xia campaign had failed, and soldiers were murmuring; on yiyou he granted graded bonuses to all armies in the capital;

sentences.zh: 既賞賚無名，士卒由是益驕。

translations.literal: since the rewards had no stated cause, the troops from this grew all the more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: because the rewards had no stated cause, the troops grew only more arrogant.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，賜錢元瓘爵吳王。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Qian Yuanguan was granted the title Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Qian Yuanguan was enfeoffed as Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 元瓘于兄弟甚厚，其兄中吳、建武節度使元璙自蘇州入見，元瓘以家人禮事之，奉觴為壽，曰：「此兄之位也，而小子居之，兄之賜也。」

translations.literal: Yuanguan was very affectionate toward his brothers; his elder brother Yuanqiao, military governor of Zhongwu and Jianwu, came from Suzhou to audience; Yuanguan received him with family ceremony, raised a cup to wish him long life, and said, "This was my elder brother's place, yet the younger brother occupies it — it is my brother's gift."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanguan was deeply devoted to his brothers; his elder brother Yuanqiao, governor of Zhongwu and Jianwu, came from Suzhou to court; Yuanguan received him with family ceremony, raised a cup in his honor, and said, "This seat was my elder brother's, yet I hold it — it is my brother's gift."

sentences.zh: 元璙曰：「先王擇賢而立之，君臣位定，元璙知忠順而已。」

translations.literal: Yuanqiao said, "Our late father chose the worthy and established him; sovereign and subject, their places are fixed — Yuanqiao knows only loyalty and obedience."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqiao said, "Our late father chose the worthy man and set him in place; sovereign and subject have their stations — I know only loyalty."

sentences.zh: 因相與對泣。

translations.literal: Thereupon they wept facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: They wept together face to face.

sentences.zh: 戊子，閩主璘復位。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the ruler of Min, Lin, resumed the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, King of Min Lin resumed the throne.

sentences.zh: 初，福建中軍使薛文傑，性巧佞，璘喜奢侈，文傑以聚使用求媚，璘以為國計使，親任之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xue Wenjie, commander of the Fujian central army, was clever and sycophantic by nature; Lin delighted in luxury, and Wenjie sought favor by amassing expenditures; Lin made him state finance commissioner and trusted him closely.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Wenjie, commander of the Fujian central army, was clever and sycophantic; Lin loved luxury, and Wenjie curried favor by squeezing revenue; Lin made him state finance commissioner and trusted him closely.

sentences.zh: 文傑陰求富民之罪，籍沒其財，被榜捶者胸背分受，仍以銅斗火熨之。

translations.literal: Wenjie secretly sought crimes among the wealthy, confiscated their property, and for those beaten with the cudgel the chest and back took the blows in turn; a heated bronze ladle was also pressed upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjie secretly framed wealthy men, confiscated their property, and had victims beaten on chest and back in turn, then seared with a heated bronze ladle.

sentences.zh: 建州土豪吳光入朝，文傑利其財，求其罪，將治之；

translations.literal: Wu Guang, a powerful local man of Jian Prefecture, came to court; Wenjie coveted his wealth, sought a crime against him, and was about to punish him;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Guang, a powerful local man of Jian Prefecture, came to court; Wenjie coveted his wealth, sought grounds to punish him,

sentences.zh: 光怨怒，帥其眾且萬人叛奔吳。

translations.literal: Guang, enraged, led his followers, nearly ten thousand strong, in rebellion and fled to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: and Guang, enraged, led nearly ten thousand followers in rebellion and fled to Wu.

sentences.zh: 帝以工部尚書盧文紀、禮部郎中呂琦為蜀王冊禮使，並賜蜀王一品朝服。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Lu Wenji, Minister of Works, and Lü Qi, Director of the Ministry of Rites, envoys for the investiture rites of the King of Shu, and also granted the King of Shu first-rank court robes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Minister of Works Lu Wenji and Ritual Director Lü Qi envoys for the King of Shu's investiture, and granted the king first-rank court robes.

sentences.zh: 知祥自作九旒冕、九章衣，車服旌旗皆擬王者。

translations.literal: Zhixiang himself had made a nine-tassel crown and nine-emblem robe; chariots, robes, banners, and flags all imitated those of a king.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang had already made a nine-tassel crown and nine-emblem robe; his chariots, dress, banners, and flags all imitated royal regalia.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙巳朔，文紀等至成都。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day yisi, Wenji and the others reached Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the first day of the month (yisi), Wenji and the others reached Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 戊申，知祥服痛冕，備儀衛詣驛，降階北面受冊，升玉輅。

translations.literal: On wushen, Zhixiang wore the mourning crown, went with full ceremonial guard to the post station, descended the steps and received the investiture facing north, then mounted the jade carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Zhixiang wore the investiture crown, went with full ceremonial guard to the post station, descended the steps to receive the investiture facing north, then mounted the jade carriage.

sentences.zh: 至府門，乘步輦而歸。

translations.literal: At the gate of his residence he took a palanquin and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At his residence gate he took a palanquin home.

sentences.zh: 文紀，簡求之孫也。

translations.literal: Wenji was a grandson of Jian Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Wenji was a grandson of Jian Qiu.

sentences.zh: 戊申，群臣上尊號曰聖明神武廣道法天文德恭孝皇帝，大赦。

translations.literal: On wushen, the ministers offered the honorific title Sagely, Illumined, Divinely Martial, Broad in the Way, Patterned in Heaven, Cultured in Virtue, and Reverently Filial Emperor, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, the ministers offered the honorific Sagely, Illumined, Divinely Martial, Broad in the Way, Patterned in Heaven, Cultured in Virtue, and Reverently Filial Emperor, and a general amnesty followed.

sentences.zh: 在京及諸道將士各等第優給。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers in the capital and in all circuits received graded special payments.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers in the capital and in every circuit received graded bonuses.

sentences.zh: 時一月之間再行優給，由是月度益窘。

translations.literal: At this time, within a single month special payments were issued again, and from this the monthly treasury grew ever more strained.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single month special payments were issued again, and the monthly treasury grew ever tighter.

sentences.zh: 太僕少卿致仕何澤見上寢疾，秦王從榮權勢方盛，冀己復進用，表請立從榮為太子。

translations.literal: He Ze, retired Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, seeing the emperor bedridden and Prince of Qin Congrong's power at its height, hoped to be employed again himself and memorialized asking that Congrong be made heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He Ze, retired Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, seeing the emperor bedridden and Prince of Qin Congrong at the height of his power, hoped to win reinstatement and memorialized to make Congrong heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 上覽表泣下，私謂左右曰：「群臣請立太子，朕當歸老太原舊第耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and wept; privately he said to those beside him, "The ministers ask to establish an heir — I should retire to my old residence at Taiyuan."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and wept; privately he told his attendants, "The ministers want an heir — I should retire to my old home at Taiyuan."

sentences.zh: 不得已，丙戌，詔宰相樞密使議之。

translations.literal: With no choice, on bingxu he ordered the chief ministers and Bureau commissioners to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: With no choice, on bingxu he ordered the chief ministers and Bureau commissioners to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，從榮見上，言曰：「竊聞有奸人請立臣為太子；

translations.literal: On dingmao, Congrong came to audience and said, "I have heard in secret that villains ask to make me heir;
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Congrong came to court and said, "I hear villains are asking to make me heir;

sentences.zh: 臣幼小，且願學治軍民，不願當此名。」

translations.literal: your servant is young, and wishes rather to learn how to govern troops and people — I do not wish to bear this title."
translations.idiomatic: I am young, and wish to learn how to govern troops and people — I do not want that title."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「群臣所欲也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "It is what the ministers desire."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is what the ministers want."

sentences.zh: 從榮退，見范延光、趙延壽曰：「執政欲以吾為太子，是欲奪我兵柄，幽之東宮耳。」

translations.literal: Congrong withdrew and said to Fan Yanguang and Zhao Shou, "The chief ministers wish to make me heir — they mean to strip me of military authority and shut me away in the Eastern Palace."
translations.idiomatic: Congrong withdrew and told Fan Yanguang and Zhao Shou, "The chief ministers want to make me heir — they mean to strip my command and shut me in the Eastern Palace."

sentences.zh: 延光等知上意，且懼從榮之言，即具以白上；

translations.literal: Yanguang and the others knew the emperor's mind and also feared Congrong's words; they reported everything to the emperor at once;
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang and the others knew the emperor's mind and feared Congrong's reaction; they reported everything at once;

sentences.zh: 辛未，制以從榮為天下兵馬大元帥。

translations.literal: on xinwei an edict made Congrong Grand Marshal of All Forces Under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: on xinwei an edict made Congrong Grand Marshal of All Forces Under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲戌朔，吳主立德妃王氏為皇后。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the first day jiaxu, the Wu ruler made Virtuous Consort Wang empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the first day of the month (jiaxu), the Wu ruler made Virtuous Consort Wang empress.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，加范延光、趙延壽兼侍中。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Fan Yanguang and Zhao Shou were given the additional title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Fan Yanguang and Zhao Shou were also named Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 癸未，中書奏節度使見元帥儀，雖帶平章事，亦以軍禮廷參，從之。

translations.literal: On guiwei, the Secretariat memorialized that when military governors attended upon the grand marshal, even if they bore the title of Associate Grand Councilor they should still pay court in military ceremony; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, the Secretariat reported that military governors attending the grand marshal, even if they held council rank, should still pay court in military ceremony; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝欲加宣徽使、判三司馮贇同平章事；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to give Feng Yun, Palace Service Commissioner and director of the Three Departments, the additional title of Associate Grand Councilor;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to make Feng Yun, Palace Service Commissioner and head of the Three Departments, Associate Grand Councilor;

sentences.zh: 贇父名章。

translations.literal: Yun's father's name was Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's father's name was Zhang.

sentences.zh: 執政誤引故事，庚寅，加贇同中書門下二品，充三司使。

translations.literal: the chief ministers mistakenly cited precedent, and on gengyin Yun was given the rank of Second Grade of the Secretariat and Chancellery and confirmed as Commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers mistakenly cited precedent, and on gengyin Yun was given Second Grade of the Secretariat and Chancellery and kept as Three Departments Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 秦王從榮請嚴衛、捧聖步騎兩指揮為牙兵。

translations.literal: Prince of Qin Congrong requested the two commands of Yanwei and Shengsheng horse and foot as his guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qin Congrong asked to have the Yanwei and Shengsheng horse and foot commands as his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 每入朝，從數百騎，張弓挾矢，馳騁衢路；

translations.literal: whenever he came to court he was followed by several hundred horsemen, bows strung and arrows at the ready, galloping through the streets;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he came to court he was followed by several hundred horsemen with bows strung and arrows ready, galloping through the streets;

sentences.zh: 令文士試草《檄淮南書》，陳己將廓清海內之意。

translations.literal: he ordered literary men to draft trial versions of a "Proclamation to Huainan," stating his intent to pacify all within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: he ordered literati to draft trial versions of a proclamation to Huainan, declaring his intent to pacify the realm.

sentences.zh: 從榮不快於執政，私謂所親曰：「吾一旦南面，必族之！」

translations.literal: Congrong was displeased with the chief ministers and privately told his intimates, "Once I face south as sovereign, I shall exterminate their clans!"
translations.idiomatic: Congrong was displeased with the chief ministers and privately told his intimates, "Once I take the throne, I shall exterminate their whole clans!"

sentences.zh: 范延光、趙延壽懼，屢求外補以避之。

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang and Zhao Shou were afraid and repeatedly sought outside appointments to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang and Zhao Shou were terrified and repeatedly sought provincial posts to escape him.

sentences.zh: 以上為見己病而求去，甚怒，曰：「欲去自去，奚用表為！」

translations.literal: Because they had seen his illness and sought to leave, he was greatly angry and said, "If you wish to go, go — why trouble with memorials!"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that they sought to leave because of his illness, he was furious and said, "If you want to go, go — why bother with memorials!"

sentences.zh: 齊國公主復為延壽言於禁中，云「延壽實有疾，不堪機務。」

translations.literal: Princess of Qi again spoke for Shou within the inner palace, saying, "Shou is truly ill and cannot bear the weight of state affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Princess of Qi again pleaded for Shou in the inner palace, saying, "Shou is truly ill and cannot manage state affairs."

sentences.zh: 丙申，二人復言於上曰：「臣等非敢憚勞，願與勳舊迭為之。

translations.literal: On bingshen the two again said to the emperor, "Your servants do not shrink from labor; we wish to rotate the duty with the meritorious elders of old.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the two again told the emperor, "We do not shrink from labor; we wish to rotate the post among the old meritocrats.

sentences.zh: 亦不敢俱去，願聽一人先出。

translations.literal: We also dare not both leave; we ask that one of us be allowed to go out first.
translations.idiomatic: We dare not both leave; let one of us go first.

sentences.zh: 若新人不稱職，復召臣，臣即至矣。」

translations.literal: If the new man is not fit for the post, recall us and we shall come at once."
translations.idiomatic: If the replacement fails, recall us and we shall return at once."

sentences.zh: 上乃許之。

translations.literal: The emperor then granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以延壽為宣武節度使；

translations.literal: On wuxu, Shou was made military governor of Xuanwu;
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Shou was appointed governor of Xuanwu;

sentences.zh: 以山南節道節度使朱弘昭為樞密使、同平章事。

translations.literal: Zhu Hongzhao, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, was made Bureau Commissioner and Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Shannan East governor Zhu Hongzhao was made Bureau Commissioner and Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 制下，弘昭復辭，上叱之曰：「汝輩皆不欲在吾側，吾蓄養汝輩何為！」

translations.literal: When the edict was issued Hongzhao declined again; the emperor rebuked him, saying, "You all do not wish to remain at my side — why have I kept and nurtured you!"
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued Hongzhao declined again; the emperor snapped, "You none of you wish to stay at my side — why have I kept you!"

sentences.zh: 弘昭乃不敢言。

translations.literal: Hongzhao then dared say no more.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao then dared say no more.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎張文寶泛海使杭州，船壞，水工以小舟濟之，風飄至天長；

translations.literal: Zhang Wenbao, Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, went by sea as envoy to Hangzhou; his ship was wrecked, and sailors ferried him in small boats until wind drove him to Tianchang;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Zhang Wenbao went by sea as envoy to Hangzhou; his ship was wrecked, sailors ferried him in small boats, and wind drove him ashore at Tianchang;

sentences.zh: 從者二百人，所存者五人。

translations.literal: of two hundred followers, only five survived.
translations.idiomatic: of two hundred followers, only five survived.

sentences.zh: 吳主厚禮之，資以從者儀服錢幣數萬，仍為之牒錢氏，使於境上迎侯。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler treated him with great courtesy, supplied his followers with regalia, robes, and coin to the amount of tens of thousands, and also issued a dispatch to the Qian clan, instructing them to receive him at the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler received him with great honor, furnished his retinue with ceremonial dress and tens of thousands in coin, and sent word to the Qian clan to meet him at the frontier.

sentences.zh: 文寶獨受飲食，餘皆辭之，曰：「本朝與吳久不通問，今既非君臣，又非賓主，若受茲物，何辭以謝！」

translations.literal: Wenbao alone accepted food and drink; all the rest declined, saying, "Our dynasty and Wu have long had no communication; now we are neither lord and subject nor host and guest — if we accept these things, with what words shall we answer!"
translations.idiomatic: Wenbao alone accepted food and drink; the others all refused, saying, "Our court and Wu have long been out of contact; we are neither sovereign and subject nor host and guest — if we took these gifts, what excuse could we offer?"

sentences.zh: 吳主嘉之，竟達命於杭州而還。

translations.literal: The Wu ruler praised this; he finally completed his mission at Hangzhou and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu ruler commended him; Wenbao finished his mission at Hangzhou and went home.

sentences.zh: 庚子，以前義成節度使李贊華為昭信節度使，留洛陽食其俸。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the former Yicheng military governor Li Zanhua was made military governor of Zhaoxin, remaining at Luoyang to draw his salary.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, former Yicheng governor Li Zanhua was appointed governor of Zhaoxin but stayed at Luoyang on full pay.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，詔大元帥從榮位在宰相上。

translations.literal: On xinchou, an edict ordered that Grand Marshal Congrong's rank be above the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, an edict placed Grand Marshal Congrong above the chief ministers in rank.

sentences.zh: 吳徐知誥以國中水火屢為災，曰：「兵民困苦，吾安可獨樂！」

translations.literal: In Wu, Xu Zhigao, because fire and flood had repeatedly struck the realm, said, "Soldiers and people are in distress — how can I alone enjoy myself!"
translations.idiomatic: In Wu, Xu Zhigao said, as fire and flood had repeatedly ravaged the realm, "Soldiers and civilians are suffering — how can I alone take pleasure!"

sentences.zh: 悉縱遣侍妓，取樂器焚之。

translations.literal: He released all his courtesans and took musical instruments and burned them.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed all his courtesans and burned his musical instruments.

sentences.zh: 閩內樞密使薛文傑說閩王抑挫諸宗室；

translations.literal: Min's Bureau Commissioner Xue Wenjie persuaded the Min ruler to suppress and humiliate the imperial clansmen;
translations.idiomatic: Min Bureau Commissioner Xue Wenjie urged the Min ruler to keep the imperial clansmen down;

sentences.zh: 從子繼圖不勝忿，謀反，坐誅，連坐者千餘人。

translations.literal: his nephew Jitu, unable to bear his resentment, plotted rebellion, was executed for the crime, and more than a thousand were implicated and punished.
translations.idiomatic: his nephew Jitu, consumed by rage, plotted revolt, was executed, and more than a thousand were punished with him.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，乙卯，范延光、馮贇奏：「西北諸胡賣馬者往來如織，日月絹無慮五千匹，計耗國用什之七，請委緣邊鎮戍擇諸胡所賣馬良者給券，具數以聞。」

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on yimao, Fan Yanguang and Feng Yun memorialized: "Barbarian horse dealers from the northwest come and go thick as weaving; each month the silk runs to no less than five thousand bolts, consuming some seven-tenths of state expenditure — we ask that border garrisons be entrusted to select the better horses sold by these barbarians, issue certificates, and report the numbers."
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on yimao, Fan Yanguang and Feng Yun submitted a memorial: "Northwestern horse traders pass back and forth like shuttles on a loom; each month we spend nearly five thousand bolts of silk — some seven-tenths of the state's costs. We ask that frontier garrisons choose the best horses offered by these tribes, issue vouchers, and report the totals."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved it.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以前武興節度使孫岳為三司使。

translations.literal: On wuwu, the former Wuxing military governor Sun Yue was made Commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, former Wuxing governor Sun Yue was appointed Commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 范延光屢因孟漢瓊、王淑妃以求出。

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang repeatedly used Meng Hanqiong and Consort Wang Shufei to seek an outside appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang repeatedly appealed through Meng Hanqiong and Consort Wang Shufei for a provincial post.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以延光為成德節度使，以馮贇為樞密使。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Yanguang was made military governor of Chengde, and Feng Yun was made Bureau Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Yanguang was sent out as governor of Chengde, and Feng Yun was made Bureau Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 帝以親軍都指揮使、同平章事康義誠為樸忠，親任之。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded Palace Guard Commander-in-Chief and Associate Grand Councilor Kang Yicheng as plain and loyal, and entrusted him closely.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw Palace Guard Commander and Associate Grand Councilor Kang Yicheng as simple and loyal, and relied on him personally.

sentences.zh: 時要近之官多求出以避秦王之禍，義誠度不能自脫，乃令其子事秦王，務以恭順持兩端，冀得自全。

translations.literal: At that time officials close to power mostly sought outside posts to escape the Prince of Qin's threat; Yicheng judged that he could not extricate himself, and so ordered his son to serve the Prince of Qin, striving to maintain both sides with respectful obedience, hoping to preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful officials at court were scrambling for provincial posts to escape the Prince of Qin; Yicheng saw no way out, so he sent his son to serve the prince, hoping to hedge with dutiful obedience and save himself.

sentences.zh: 權知夏州事李彝超上表謝罪，求昭雪；

translations.literal: Li Yichao, acting administrator of Xia Prefecture, submitted a memorial asking pardon and seeking rehabilitation;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yichao, acting administrator of Xia Prefecture, submitted a memorial of apology and asked to be cleared;

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以彝超為定難軍節充使。

translations.literal: On renxu, Yichao was made military governor of the Dingnan army.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Yichao was confirmed as military governor of Dingnan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲戌，上餞范延光，酒罷，上曰：「卿今遠去，事宜盡言。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiaxu, the emperor gave a farewell banquet for Fan Yanguang; when the wine was finished, the emperor said, "You are going far away — matters should be spoken fully."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiaxu, the emperor gave Fan Yanguang a farewell banquet; when the wine was done, he said, "You are going far off — speak plainly about whatever needs saying."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「朝廷大事，願陛下與內久輔臣參決，勿聽群小之言。」

translations.literal: He answered, "On great affairs of state, I wish Your Majesty would consult and decide with the long-serving inner ministers — do not heed the words of petty men."
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang replied, "On great matters of state, I beg Your Majesty to decide with your senior inner ministers — do not listen to petty men."

sentences.zh: 遂相泣而別。

translations.literal: They then wept facing each other and parted.
translations.idiomatic: They wept together and parted.

sentences.zh: 時孟漢瓊用事，附之者共為朋黨以蔽惑上聽，故延光言及之。

translations.literal: At that time Meng Hanqiong held power; those who attached to him formed factions together to screen and mislead what reached the emperor's ears — hence Yanguang spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Hanqiong then held sway; his followers had formed a faction that screened the emperor's ears, which was why Yanguang had said what he did.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，改慎州懷化軍。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Shen Prefecture was renamed the Huaihua garrison.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Shen Prefecture was redesignated the Huaihua garrison.

sentences.zh: 置保順軍於洮州，領洮、鄯等州。

translations.literal: The Baoshun garrison was established at Tao Prefecture, overseeing Tao, Shan, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The Baoshun garrison was set up at Tao Prefecture, with jurisdiction over Tao, Shan, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 戊子，帝疾復作，己丑，大漸，秦王從榮入問疾，帝俯首不能舉。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the emperor's illness recurred; on jichou, he sank critically; Prince of Qin Congrong entered to inquire after his health — the emperor bowed his head and could not raise it.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the emperor's illness returned; on jichou he was near death. Prince of Qin Congrong came to inquire after him, but the emperor could only bow his head and could not lift it.

sentences.zh: 王淑妃曰：「從榮在此。」

translations.literal: Consort Wang Shufei said, "Congrong is here."
translations.idiomatic: Consort Wang Shufei said, "Congrong is here."

sentences.zh: 帝不應。

translations.literal: The emperor did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not respond.

sentences.zh: 從榮出，聞宮中皆哭，從榮意帝已殂，明旦，稱疾不入。

translations.literal: Congrong went out, heard weeping throughout the palace, and thought the emperor had died; the next morning he claimed illness and did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Congrong left, heard weeping throughout the palace, and took it that the emperor was dead; the next morning he pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 是夕，帝實小愈，而從榮不知。

translations.literal: That evening the emperor had in fact slightly improved, but Congrong did not know.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor had in fact rallied slightly, but Congrong did not know it.

sentences.zh: 從榮自知不為時論所與，恐不得為嗣，與其黨謀，欲以兵入侍，先制權臣。
