translations.literal: Congrong knew himself not supported by current opinion and feared he would not become heir; with his faction he plotted to enter with troops to attend the emperor and first seize the powerful ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Congrong knew public opinion was against him and feared he would not succeed; with his followers he plotted to force his way in with troops, attend the emperor, and first overpower the power-holders.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，從榮遣都押牙馬處鈞謂朱弘昭、馮贇曰：「吾欲帥牙兵入宮中侍疾，且備非常，當止於何所？」

translations.literal: On xinmao, Congrong sent Chief Adjutant Ma Chujun to tell Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun, "I wish to lead my guard troops into the palace to attend the illness and guard against the unexpected — where should we halt?"
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Congrong sent Chief Adjutant Ma Chujun to Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun with this message: "I mean to lead my guard into the palace to attend the illness and guard against trouble — where should we stop?"

sentences.zh: 二人曰：「王自擇之。」

translations.literal: The two said, "The Prince may choose for himself."
translations.idiomatic: The two replied, "Your Highness may choose for yourself."

sentences.zh: 既而私於處鈞曰：「主上萬福，王宜竭心忠孝，不可妄信人浮言。」

translations.literal: Then privately they told Chujun, "The emperor enjoys boundless fortune — the Prince should devote his heart to loyalty and filial piety and must not lightly believe people's idle talk."
translations.idiomatic: Then they told Chujun privately, "His Majesty enjoys boundless fortune; the prince should give himself wholly to loyalty and filial piety and not heed idle rumor."

sentences.zh: 從榮怒，復遣處鈞謂二人曰：「公輩殊不愛家族邪？

translations.literal: Congrong was angry and again sent Chujun to tell the two, "Do you gentlemen not love your families at all?
translations.idiomatic: Congrong was furious and sent Chujun back: "Do you people care nothing for your families?

sentences.zh: 何敢拒我！」

translations.literal: How dare you reject me!"
translations.idiomatic: How dare you refuse me!"

sentences.zh: 二人患之，入告王淑妃及宣徽使孟漢瓊，鹹曰：「茲事不得康義誠不可濟。」

translations.literal: The two were troubled by this; they entered and reported to Consort Wang Shufei and Palace Service Commissioner Meng Hanqiong; all said, "This affair cannot succeed without Kang Yicheng."
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, the two reported to Consort Wang Shufei and Palace Service Commissioner Meng Hanqiong; all agreed, "This cannot be done without Kang Yicheng."

sentences.zh: 乃召義誠謀之，義誠竟無言，但曰：「義誠，將校耳，不敢預議，惟相公所使。」

translations.literal: They then summoned Yicheng to plan; Yicheng ultimately said nothing, but only, "Yicheng is a mere field officer — I dare not take part in deliberation; I await whatever the lords command."
translations.idiomatic: They summoned Yicheng to counsel with them; he said almost nothing, only, "Yicheng is a mere field officer — I dare not join deliberation; I await your orders."

sentences.zh: 弘昭疑義誠不欲眾中言之，夜，邀至私第問之，其對如初。

translations.literal: Hongzhao suspected Yicheng did not wish to speak before the assembly; at night he invited him to his private residence and questioned him — his answer was as before.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao suspected Yicheng would not speak openly before the group; that night he invited him home and questioned him again, and got the same answer.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，從榮自河南府常服將步騎千人陳於天津橋。

translations.literal: On renchen, Congrong, in ordinary dress from Henan Prefecture, led a thousand infantry and cavalry and drew them up at Tianjin Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Congrong left Henan Prefecture in plain clothes at the head of a thousand foot and horse, and formed them at Tianjin Bridge.

sentences.zh: 是日黎明，從榮遣馬處鈞至馮贇第，語之曰：「吾今日決入，且居興聖宮。

translations.literal: That day at dawn, Congrong sent Ma Chujun to Feng Yun's residence and told him, "Today I am resolved to enter, and shall lodge at Xingsheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn that day Congrong sent Ma Chujun to Feng Yun's house with word: "I am going in today and will take up residence in Xingsheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 公輩各有宗族，處事亦宜詳允，禍福在須臾耳。」

translations.literal: You gentlemen each have clans — in handling affairs you should also consider carefully; fortune and disaster hang in a moment."
translations.idiomatic: You all have families; handle this with care — fortune and ruin hang on an instant."

sentences.zh: 又遣處鈞詣康義誠，義誠曰：「王為則奉迎。」

translations.literal: He also sent Chujun to Kang Yicheng; Yicheng said, "If the Prince acts, I shall welcome him."
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Chujun to Kang Yicheng, who said, "If the prince moves, I shall receive him."

sentences.zh: 贇馳入右掖門，見弘昭、義誠、漢瓊及三司使孫岳方聚謀於中興殿門外，贇具道處鈞之言，因讓義誠曰：「秦王言『禍福在須臾，』其事可知，公勿以兒在秦府，左右顧望。

translations.literal: Feng Yun galloped in through the Right Wing Gate and saw Hongzhao, Yicheng, Hanqiong, and Commissioner of the Three Departments Sun Yue gathered in consultation outside the Zhongxing Hall gate; Yun fully reported Chujun's words and rebuked Yicheng, saying, "The Prince of Qin says, 'Fortune and disaster hang in a moment' — the meaning is clear; do not, because your son is in the Qin prince's household, look this way and that.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yun galloped in through the Right Wing Gate and found Hongzhao, Yicheng, Hanqiong, and Commissioner of the Three Departments Sun Yue conferring outside the Zhongxing Hall. Yun repeated Chujun's message and rebuked Yicheng: "When the Prince of Qin says 'fortune and ruin hang on an instant,' his meaning is plain — do not hedge because your son serves in the Qin household.

sentences.zh: 主上拔擢吾輩，自布衣至將相，苟使秦王兵得入此門，置主上何地？

translations.literal: The emperor raised us from common cloth to general and chancellor — if the Prince of Qin's troops should enter this gate, where would that leave the emperor?
translations.idiomatic: His Majesty raised us from commoners to generals and chancellors — if the Prince of Qin's troops pass this gate, where will that leave the emperor?

sentences.zh: 吾輩尚有遺種乎？」

translations.literal: Would any seed of us remain?"
translations.idiomatic: Will any of our families survive?"

sentences.zh: 義誠未及對，監門白秦王已將兵至端門外。

translations.literal: Before Yicheng could answer, the gate warden reported that the Prince of Qin had already brought troops to outside the Duan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Before Yicheng could reply, the gate warden announced that the Prince of Qin had already brought troops to the Duan Gate.

sentences.zh: 漢瓊指衣起曰：「今日之事，危及君父，公猶顧望擇利邪？

translations.literal: Hanqiong pointed at his robe and rose, saying, "Today's affair threatens lord and father — and you still look this way and that, choosing profit?
translations.idiomatic: Hanqiong pointed at his robe and stood, saying, "Today's crisis threatens lord and father — and you still hesitate, weighing gain?

sentences.zh: 吾何愛餘生，當自帥兵拒之耳！」

translations.literal: Why should I cherish the years left to me — I shall lead troops myself to resist him!"
translations.idiomatic: Why should I cling to what life remains — I will lead troops myself to stop him!"

sentences.zh: 即入殿門，弘照、贇隨之，義誠不得已，亦隨之入。

translations.literal: He at once entered the hall gate; Hongzhao and Yun followed; Yicheng, having no choice, followed as well.
translations.idiomatic: He went straight through the hall gate; Hongzhao and Yun followed, and Yicheng, with no choice, went in after them.

sentences.zh: 漢瓊見帝曰：「從榮反，兵已攻端門，須臾入宮，則大亂矣！」

translations.literal: Hanqiong saw the emperor and said, "Congrong has rebelled — his troops have already assaulted the Duan Gate; in a moment they will enter the palace and great disorder will ensue!"
translations.idiomatic: Hanqiong saw the emperor and said, "Congrong has rebelled — his troops are already at the Duan Gate; in a moment they will enter the palace and all will be chaos!"

sentences.zh: 宮中相顧號哭，帝曰：「從榮何苦乃爾！」

translations.literal: Within the palace they looked at one another and wailed; the emperor said, "Why must Congrong be so tormented!"
translations.idiomatic: Inside the palace everyone looked at one another and wailed; the emperor said, "Why must Congrong come to this!"

sentences.zh: 問弘昭等：「有諸？」

translations.literal: He asked Hongzhao and the others, "Is it so?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked Hongzhao and the others, "Is it true?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「有之，適已令門者闔門矣。」

translations.literal: They answered, "It is so — we have just ordered the gatekeepers to shut the gates."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "It is — we have just ordered the gates shut."

sentences.zh: 帝指天泣下，謂義誠曰：「卿自處置，勿驚百姓！」

translations.literal: The emperor pointed to heaven and wept, telling Yicheng, "Handle it yourself — do not alarm the people!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pointed heavenward and wept, telling Yicheng, "Deal with it yourself — do not frighten the people!"

sentences.zh: 控鶴指揮使李重吉，從珂之子也，時侍側，帝曰：「吾與爾父，冒矢石定天下，數脫吾於厄；

translations.literal: Palace Crane Commander Li Chongji — Congke's son — was then attending at the emperor's side; the emperor said, "Your father and I braved arrow and stone to settle the realm and repeatedly delivered me from peril;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Crane Commander Li Chongji — Li Congke's son — was then at the emperor's side. The emperor said, "Your father and I braved arrow and stone to settle the realm and again and again pulled me from disaster;

sentences.zh: 從榮輩得何力，今乃為人所教，為此悖逆！

translations.literal: What strength had Congrong's sort? Now he has been taught by others to commit this outrage!
translations.idiomatic: what strength had Congrong's crowd ever shown? Now others have taught him this outrage!

sentences.zh: 我固知此曹不足付大事，當呼爾父授以兵柄耳。

translations.literal: I always knew this lot could not be entrusted with great affairs — I should summon your father and give him the military command.
translations.idiomatic: I always knew this lot could not be trusted with great affairs — I ought to summon your father and give him command of the armies.

sentences.zh: 汝為我部閉諸門。」

translations.literal: You shall deploy for me and shut all the gates.
translations.idiomatic: You — deploy for me and shut every gate."

sentences.zh: 重吉即帥控鶴兵守宮門。

translations.literal: Chongji at once led the Palace Crane troops to guard the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Chongji at once led the Palace Crane troops to hold the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 孟漢瓊被甲乘馬，召馬軍都指揮使朱洪實，使將五百騎討從榮。

translations.literal: Meng Hanqiong donned armor, mounted a horse, summoned Cavalry Commander Zhu Hongshi, and had him lead five hundred horsemen to suppress Congrong.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Hanqiong put on armor, mounted a horse, summoned Cavalry Commander Zhu Hongshi, and ordered him to take five hundred horsemen against Congrong.

sentences.zh: 從榮方據胡床，坐橋上，遣左右召康義誠。

translations.literal: Congrong was just occupying a folding stool, seated on the bridge, and sent attendants to summon Kang Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Congrong was lounging on a folding stool on the bridge and sent attendants to summon Kang Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 端門已閉，叩左掖門，從門隙中窺之，見朱洪實引騎兵北來，走白從榮。

translations.literal: The Duan Gate was already shut; they knocked at the Left Wing Gate and peeped through the gate crack — they saw Zhu Hongshi leading cavalry northward and ran to tell Congrong.
translations.idiomatic: The Duan Gate was already shut; they knocked at the Left Wing Gate, peered through the crack, saw Zhu Hongshi leading cavalry northward, and ran to tell Congrong.

sentences.zh: 從榮大驚，命取鐵掩心擐之，坐調弓矢。

translations.literal: Congrong was greatly alarmed; he ordered iron heart-guards fetched and donned, and sat adjusting bow and arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Congrong was badly shaken; he had an iron breastplate brought and put on, and sat tuning bow and arrow.

sentences.zh: 俄而騎兵大至，從榮走歸府，僚佐皆竄匿，牙兵掠嘉善坊潰去。

translations.literal: Soon cavalry arrived in force; Congrong fled back to his residence; his staff all hid themselves; his guard troops plundered Jiahe Ward and broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon cavalry arrived in force; Congrong fled to his residence; his staff scattered and hid; his guard troops looted Jiahe Ward and broke away.

sentences.zh: 從榮與妃劉氏匿床下，皇城使安從益就斬之，並殺其子，以其首獻。

translations.literal: Congrong and his consort Lady Liu hid under the bed; Imperial City Commissioner An Congyi went and beheaded him, also killed his son, and presented their heads.
translations.idiomatic: Congrong and his consort Lady Liu hid under a bed; Imperial City Commissioner An Congyi went in and beheaded him, killed his son as well, and presented their heads.

sentences.zh: 初，孫岳頗得豫內廷密謀，馮、朱患從榮狼伉，岳嘗為之極言禍福之歸；

translations.literal: Earlier, Sun Yue had largely taken part in the inner court's secret counsel; Feng and Zhu feared Congrong's unruliness, and Yue had often spoken at length to him on where fortune and disaster lay;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sun Yue had been privy to the inner court's secret plans; Feng and Zhu feared Congrong's unruliness, and Yue had often warned him plainly where fortune and ruin would lead;

sentences.zh: 康義誠恨之，至是，乘亂密遣騎士射殺之。

translations.literal: Kang Yicheng resented this; at this juncture, amid the turmoil, he secretly sent horsemen to shoot and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yicheng resented this; now, amid the chaos, he secretly sent horsemen to shoot Yue dead.

sentences.zh: 帝聞從榮死，悲駭，幾落御榻，絕而復甦者再，由是疾復劇。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard Congrong was dead, he was stricken with grief and shock — he nearly fell from the imperial couch, twice losing consciousness and reviving; from this his illness grew worse again.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard Congrong was dead, grief and shock nearly threw him from the imperial couch; he lost consciousness twice and came back; from then on his illness worsened again.

sentences.zh: 從榮一子尚幼，養宮中，諸將請除之，帝泣曰：「此何罪！」

translations.literal: Congrong had one son still young, being raised in the palace; the generals asked that he be eliminated; the emperor wept and said, "What crime is this!"
translations.idiomatic: Congrong had one young son being raised in the palace; the generals asked that he be killed too; the emperor wept and said, "What crime has he committed!"

sentences.zh: 不得已，竟與之。

translations.literal: Having no choice, he finally yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to refuse, he finally consented.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，馮道帥群臣入見帝於雍和殿，帝雨泣嗚咽，曰：「吾家事至此，慚見卿等！」

translations.literal: On guisi, Feng Dao led the ministers in to see the emperor at Yonghe Hall; the emperor wept in streaming tears and sobs, saying, "My household affairs have come to this — I am ashamed to face you!"
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Feng Dao led the ministers in to see the emperor in Yonghe Hall; the emperor wept aloud and said, "My house has come to this — I am ashamed to face you!"

sentences.zh: 宋王從厚為天雄節度使；

translations.literal: Prince of Song Conghou was made military governor of Tianxiong;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Song Conghou was made governor of Tianxiong;

sentences.zh: 甲午，遣孟漢瓊征從厚，且權知天雄軍府事。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Meng Hanqiong was dispatched to campaign against Conghou and also made acting administrator of the Tianxiong headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Meng Hanqiong was sent to campaign against Conghou and also made acting administrator of the Tianxiong headquarters.

sentences.zh: 丙申，追廢從榮為庶人。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Congrong was posthumously degraded to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Congrong was posthumously stripped of rank and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 執政共議從榮官屬之罪，馮道曰：「從榮所親者高輦、劉陟、王說而已，任贊到官才半月，王居敏、司徒詡在病告已半年，豈豫其謀！

translations.literal: The chief ministers jointly deliberated on the guilt of Congrong's staff; Feng Dao said, "Those Congrong was close to were only Gao Nian, Liu Zhi, and Wang Yue; Ren Zan had been in office only half a month; Wang Jumin and Situ Xu had been on sick leave for half a year — how could they have joined the plot!
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers jointly debated the guilt of Congrong's staff; Feng Dao said, "Congrong's intimates were only Gao Nian, Liu Zhi, and Wang Yue; Ren Zan had been in office barely half a month; Wang Jumin and Situ Xu had been on sick leave for half a year — how could they have joined the plot!

sentences.zh: 居敏尤為從榮所惡，昨舉兵向闕之際，與輦、陟並轡而行，指日景曰：『來日及今，已誅王詹事矣。』

translations.literal: Jumin was especially hated by Congrong; when troops were raised yesterday toward the palace, he rode alongside Gao Nian and Liu Zhi, pointed at the sun's shadow, and said, 'By tomorrow at this hour, the Crown Prince's Tutor will already have been executed.'
translations.idiomatic: Jumin was especially hated by Congrong; when the troops marched on the palace yesterday, he rode alongside Gao Nian and Liu Zhi, pointed at the sun's shadow, and said, 'By this hour tomorrow the Crown Prince's Tutor will already be dead.'

sentences.zh: 自非與之同謀者，豈得一切誅之乎！」

translations.literal: If he were not of one plot with them, could all alike be put to death!"
translations.idiomatic: If he were not in league with them, how could all alike be put to death!"

sentences.zh: 朱弘昭曰：「使從榮得入光政門，贊等當如何任使，而吾輩猶有利乎！

translations.literal: Zhu Hongzhao said, "If Congrong had entered the Guangzheng Gate, how would Zan and the others have been employed — and would we still have had any advantage!
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongzhao said, "If Congrong had entered the Guangzheng Gate, how would Zan and the rest have been used — and would we still have come out ahead!

sentences.zh: 且首從差一等耳，今首已孥戮而從皆不問，主上能不以吾輩為庇奸人乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover, ringleader and follower differ by one degree — now the ringleader has been executed with his family while followers are not questioned; will the emperor not take us for shielding wrongdoers!"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, ringleader and follower differ by one degree — the ringleader is already executed with his family while followers go unpunished; will His Majesty not think we are shielding criminals!"

sentences.zh: 馮贇力爭之，始議流貶。

translations.literal: Feng Yun argued forcefully, and exile was finally agreed upon.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yun argued hard, and exile was finally agreed on.

sentences.zh: 時咨議高輦已伏誅。

translations.literal: At that time Adviser Gao Nian had already been executed.
translations.idiomatic: By then Adviser Gao Nian had already been executed.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，元帥府判官、兵部侍郎任贊、秘書監兼王傅劉瓚、友蘇瓚、記室魚崇遠、河南少尹劉陟、判官司徒詡、推官王說等八人並長流，河南巡官李瀚、江文蔚等六人勒歸田裡，六軍判官、太子詹事王居敏、推官郭晙並貶官。

translations.literal: On dingyou, eight men — Grand Marshal's staff judge Ren Zan, Vice Minister of War; Secretariat Director and Crown Prince Tutor Liu Zan; companion Su Zan; recorder Yu Chongyuan; Henan Vice Governor Liu Zhi; staff judge Situ Xu; and staff officer Wang Yue — were all sentenced to distant exile; six including Henan patrol officer Li Han and Jiang Wenwei were compelled to return to their home villages; Six Armies staff judge and Crown Prince Tutor Wang Jumin and staff officer Guo Jun were all demoted.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, eight men — Grand Marshal staff judge and Vice Minister of War Ren Zan; Secretariat Director and Crown Prince Tutor Liu Zan; companion Su Zan; recorder Yu Chongyuan; Henan Vice Governor Liu Zhi; staff judge Situ Xu; and staff officer Wang Yue — were sentenced to distant exile; six men including Henan patrol officer Li Han and Jiang Wenwei were ordered home to their villages; Six Armies staff judge and Crown Prince Tutor Wang Jumin and staff officer Guo Jun were demoted.

sentences.zh: 瀚，回之族曾孫也；

translations.literal: Han was a great-great-grandson of Han Hui;
translations.idiomatic: Li Han was a great-great-grandson of Han Hui;

sentences.zh: 詡，貝州人；

translations.literal: Xu was a native of Beizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Situ Xu was from Beizhou;

sentences.zh: 文蔚，建安人也。

translations.literal: Wenwei was a native of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wenwei was from Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 文蔚奔吳，徐知誥厚禮之。

translations.literal: Wenwei fled to Wu, and Xu Zhigao treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei fled to Wu, where Xu Zhigao received him with great honor.

sentences.zh: 初，從榮失道，六軍判官、司諫郎中趙遠諫曰：「大王地居上嗣，當勤修令德，奈何所為如是！

translations.literal: Earlier, when Congrong had lost the Way, Six Armies staff judge and Remonstrance Bureau Director Zhao Yuan admonished him, saying, "The Great Prince stands as heir apparent — you should diligently cultivate fine virtue; why conduct yourself thus!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Congrong had lost his way, Six Armies staff judge and Remonstrance Bureau Director Zhao Yuan admonished him: "Your Highness stands as heir — you should diligently cultivate virtue; why behave like this!

sentences.zh: 勿謂父子至親為可恃，獨不見恭世子、戾太子乎！」

translations.literal: Do not think that the utmost closeness of father and son is something to rely on — have you alone not seen the case of Crown Prince Gong and Crown Prince Li!"
translations.idiomatic: Do not think the closeness of father and son is something you can rely on — have you never heard of Crown Prince Gong and Crown Prince Li!"

sentences.zh: 從榮怒，出為涇州判官；

translations.literal: Congrong was angry and sent him out as judge of Jing Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Congrong was furious and sent him out as judge of Jing Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 及從榮敗，遠以是知名。

translations.literal: When Congrong was defeated, Yuan became famous for this.
translations.idiomatic: When Congrong fell, Yuan became famous for it.

sentences.zh: 遠，字上交，幽州人也。

translations.literal: Yuan, styled Shangjiao, was a native of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yuan, styled Shangjiao, was from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，帝殂。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 帝性不猜忌，與物無競，登極之年已逾六十，每夕於宮中焚香祝天曰：「某胡人，因亂為眾所推；

translations.literal: The emperor's nature was free of suspicion; he did not contend with others; the year he ascended the throne he was already past sixty; each evening in the palace he burned incense and prayed to Heaven, saying, "I, a certain Hu man, was pushed forward by the multitude amid turmoil;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was free of suspicion and did not contend with others; he was already past sixty when he took the throne; each evening in the palace he burned incense and prayed to Heaven, saying, "I, a certain Hu man, was raised up by the multitude in chaos;

sentences.zh: 願天早生聖人，為生民主。」

translations.literal: May Heaven soon produce a sage to be lord and master of the living people."
translations.idiomatic: may Heaven soon send a sage to rule the people."

sentences.zh: 在位年谷屢豐，兵革罕用，校於五代，粗為小康。

translations.literal: During his reign harvests were repeatedly abundant and arms were rarely used; compared with the Five Dynasties period, it was roughly a modest peace.
translations.idiomatic: During his reign harvests were often plentiful and war was seldom waged; measured against the Five Dynasties, his age was a modest peace.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，宋王至洛陽。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the Prince of Song reached Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, the Prince of Song reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 閩主尊魯國太夫人黃氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: The Min ruler honored Lady Huang, Grand Matron of Lu, as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler honored Lady Huang, Grand Matron of Lu, as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 閩主好鬼神，巫盛韜等皆有寵。

translations.literal: The Min ruler favored spirits and ghosts; shamans such as Sheng Tao all enjoyed favor.
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler doted on spirits and ghosts; shamans such as Sheng Tao all enjoyed favor.

sentences.zh: 薛文傑言於閩主曰：「陛下左右多奸臣，非質諸鬼神，不能知也。

translations.literal: Xue Wenjie said to the Min ruler, "Among those at Your Majesty's side are many treacherous ministers — unless the matter is tested before the spirits and ghosts, it cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Wenjie said to the Min ruler, "Your Majesty is surrounded by treacherous ministers — unless the truth is tested before the spirits, it cannot be known.

sentences.zh: 盛韜善視鬼，宜使察之。」

translations.literal: Sheng Tao is skilled at seeing ghosts; he should be sent to investigate them."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Tao is skilled at seeing ghosts — he should be sent to investigate."

sentences.zh: 閩主從之。

translations.literal: The Min ruler followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler agreed.

sentences.zh: 文傑惡樞密使吳勖，勖在疾，文傑省之，曰：「主上以公久疾，欲罷公近密，僕言公但小苦頭痛耳，將愈矣。

translations.literal: Wenjie hated Bureau Commissioner Wu Xu; Xu was ill, and Wenjie visited him, saying, "The ruler, seeing that you have been ill for long, wishes to remove you from close confidential service; I told him you suffer only a little from headache and will soon recover.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjie hated Bureau Commissioner Wu Xu. Xu lay ill, and Wenjie visited him, saying, "The ruler, seeing your long illness, wishes to remove you from his inner circle. I told him you suffer only a slight headache and will soon recover.

sentences.zh: 主上或遣使來問，慎勿以它疾對也。」

translations.literal: If the ruler should send an envoy to inquire, take care not to answer with some other illness.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler sends someone to inquire, be careful not to mention any other ailment."

sentences.zh: 勖許諾。

translations.literal: Xu promised.
translations.idiomatic: Xu agreed.

sentences.zh: 明日，文傑使韜言於閩主曰：「適見北廟崇順王訊吳勖謀反，以銅釘釘其腦，金椎擊之。」

translations.literal: The next day Wenjie had Tao speak to the Min ruler, saying, "Just now at the Northern Temple I saw Prince Chongshun interrogating Wu Xu for plotting rebellion — copper nails were driven into his brain and beaten with a golden mace.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Wenjie had Tao tell the Min ruler, "I have just seen at the Northern Temple Prince Chongshun interrogating Wu Xu for plotting rebellion — copper nails driven into his brain, beaten with a golden mace.

sentences.zh: 閩主以告文傑，文傑曰：「未可信也，宜遣使問之。」

translations.literal: The Min ruler reported this to Wenjie; Wenjie said, "This cannot yet be trusted; an envoy should be sent to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler told Wenjie, who said, "That cannot be trusted yet — send an envoy to inquire.

sentences.zh: 果以頭痛對，即收下獄，遣文傑及獄吏雜治之，勖自誣服，並其妻子誅之。

translations.literal: Xu indeed answered with headache; he was immediately arrested and imprisoned; Wenjie and prison officers jointly tortured him; Xu falsely confessed of his own accord, and he and his wife and children were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu indeed answered that he had a headache. He was arrested at once and thrown into prison; Wenjie and the jailers tortured him together until Xu falsely confessed — he and his wife and children were all executed.

sentences.zh: 由是國人益怒。

translations.literal: From this the people of the state grew only angrier.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Min grew only angrier.

sentences.zh: 吳光請兵於吳，吳信州刺史蔣延徽不俟朝命，引兵會光攻建州，閩主遣使求救於吳越。

translations.literal: Wu Guang requested troops from Wu; Wu's Xin Prefecture governor Jiang Yanhui, without awaiting court orders, led troops to join Guang in attacking Jian Prefecture; the Min ruler sent envoys seeking rescue from Wuyue.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Guang asked Wu for troops; Xin Prefecture governor Jiang Yanhui, without waiting for court orders, led his army to join Guang in attacking Jian Prefecture — the Min ruler sent envoys to Wuyue begging for aid.

sentences.zh: 十二月，癸卯朔，始發明宗喪，宋王即皇帝位。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day of the month (guimao), Mingzong's funeral procession began; the Prince of Song took the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the first day of the month (guimao), Mingzong's funeral procession set out, and the Prince of Song ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 秦王從榮既死，朱洪實妻入宮，司衣王氏與之語及秦王，王氏曰：「秦王為人子，不在左右侍疾，致人歸禍，是其罪也；

translations.literal: After Prince of Qin Congrong had died, Zhu Hongshi's wife entered the palace; Palace Attendant of Robes Lady Wang spoke with her about the Prince of Qin, and Lady Wang said, "The Prince of Qin, as a son, was not at his father's side tending his illness and brought disaster upon others — that is his crime;
translations.idiomatic: After Prince of Qin Congrong's death, Zhu Hongshi's wife entered the palace. Palace Attendant Lady Wang spoke with her about the prince, saying, "As a son, the Prince of Qin was not at his father's bedside in illness and brought calamity upon others — that was his crime;

sentences.zh: 若雲大逆，則厚誣矣。

translations.literal: if one calls it great treason, that is a gross false charge.
translations.idiomatic: to call it treason would be a gross false charge.

sentences.zh: 朱司徒最受王恩，當時不為之辨，惜哉！」

translations.literal: Minister Zhu received the greatest royal favor — that he did not speak in his defense at the time is a pity!
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhu received the greatest favor from the late emperor — that he did not speak in the prince's defense then is a pity!"

sentences.zh: 洪實聞之，大懼，與康義誠以其語白閔帝，且言王氏私於從榮，為之詗宮中事，辛亥，賜王氏死。

translations.literal: Hongshi heard this and was greatly afraid; with Kang Yicheng he reported her words to Emperor Min, also saying Lady Wang had been intimate with Congrong and spied on palace affairs for him; on xinhai, Lady Wang was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Hongshi heard of this and was terrified. He and Kang Yicheng reported her words to Emperor Min, adding that Lady Wang had been intimate with Congrong and spied on palace affairs for him. On xinhai, Lady Wang was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 事連王淑妃，淑妃素厚於從榮，帝由是疑之。

translations.literal: The affair implicated Consort Wang Shufei; Shufei had long been close to Congrong, and the emperor from this grew suspicious of her.
translations.idiomatic: The affair implicated Consort Wang Shufei, who had long been close to Congrong — the emperor grew suspicious of her.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以天雄左都押牙宋令詢為磁州刺史。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Song Lingxun, Left Chief adjutant of Tianxiong, was made governor of Ci Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Song Lingxun, Left Chief adjutant of Tianxiong, was appointed governor of Ci Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 朱弘昭以誅秦王立帝為己功，欲專朝政；

translations.literal: Zhu Hongzhao took the slaying of the Prince of Qin and enthronement of the emperor as his own achievement and wished to monopolize court governance;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongzhao counted the slaying of the Prince of Qin and the emperor's enthronement as his own achievement and sought to monopolize court governance;

sentences.zh: 令詢侍帝左右最久，雅為帝所親信，弘昭不欲舊人在帝側，故出之。

translations.literal: Lingxun had attended the emperor's side longest and was greatly trusted by him; Hongzhao did not want old associates at the emperor's side and therefore sent him out.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxun had attended the emperor longest and was deeply trusted; Hongzhao wanted no old intimates at the emperor's side and therefore had him sent out.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅而無如之何。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased but could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased but could do nothing.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥聞明宗殂，謂僚佐曰：「宋王幼弱，為政者皆胥史小人，其亂可坐俟也。」

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang, hearing that Mingzong had died, said to his staff, "The Prince of Song is young and weak; those who govern are all petty clerk scribes — their disorder can be awaited sitting down."
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Zhixiang heard that Mingzong had died, he told his staff, "The Prince of Song is young and weak, and those who hold power are petty clerk scribes — their collapse can be awaited sitting down."

sentences.zh: 辛未，帝始御中興殿。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the emperor first held court in the Zhongxing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, the emperor held his first audience in the Zhongxing Hall.

sentences.zh: 帝自終易月之制，即召學士讀《貞觀政要》、《太宗實錄》，有致治之志；

translations.literal: Since ending the observance of mourning garb, the emperor at once summoned academicians to read the Essentials of Governance from the Zhenguan Reign and the Veritable Record of Emperor Taizong, harboring the will to bring good order;
translations.idiomatic: As soon as mourning garb ended, the emperor summoned academicians to read the Essentials of Governance from the Zhenguan Reign and the Veritable Record of Emperor Taizong — he harbored the will to bring good order;

sentences.zh: 然不知其要，寬柔少斷。

translations.literal: yet he did not grasp the essentials — lenient, gentle, and seldom decisive.
translations.idiomatic: yet he did not grasp what mattered — lenient, gentle, and seldom decisive.

sentences.zh: 李愚私謂同列曰：「吾君延訪，鮮及吾輩，位高責重，事亦堪憂。」

translations.literal: Li Yu privately said to his colleagues, "Our lord extends inquiries, yet rarely reaches us — our positions are high and responsibilities heavy; the matter is also worth worry.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu privately told his colleagues, "Our lord holds audiences, yet rarely seeks us out — with rank so high and responsibility so heavy, the situation gives cause for worry.

sentences.zh: 眾惕息不敢應。

translations.literal: The group held their breath in fear and dared not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The others held their breath and dared not reply.

sentences.zh: 順化節度使、同平章事、判明州錢元珦驕縱不法，每請事於王府不獲，輒上書悖慢。

translations.literal: Shunhua governor, Associate Grand Councilor, and administrator of Ming Prefecture Qian Yuanxiang was arrogant, unruly, and lawless; whenever he petitioned the princely headquarters and did not obtain his wish, he would submit memorials that were insolent and contemptuous.
translations.idiomatic: Shunhua governor, Associate Grand Councilor, and administrator of Ming Prefecture Qian Yuanxiang was arrogant and lawless; whenever his petitions to the princely headquarters were denied, he submitted insolent, contemptuous memorials.

sentences.zh: 嘗怒一吏，置鐵床炙之，臭滿城郭。

translations.literal: Once in anger against a clerk he set an iron bed and roasted him on it; the stench filled the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Once, enraged at a clerk, he had him roasted on an iron bed — the stench filled the city.

sentences.zh: 吳王元瓘遣牙將仰仁詮詣明州召之，仁詮左右慮元珦難制，勸為之備，仁詮不從，常服徑造聽事。

translations.literal: King of Wu Yuanqian sent gate officer Yang Renquan to Ming Prefecture to summon him; Renquan's attendants feared Yuanxiang would be hard to control and urged preparations; Renquan would not listen and in ordinary dress went straight to the headquarters reception hall.
translations.idiomatic: King of Wu Yuanqian sent gate officer Yang Renquan to Ming Prefecture to summon him. Renquan's attendants feared Yuanxiang would resist and urged precautions, but Renquan refused and went straight to headquarters in plain dress.

sentences.zh: 元珦見仁詮至，股心栗，遂還錢塘，幽於別第。

translations.literal: Yuanxiang, seeing Renquan arrive, trembled in thigh and heart; he then returned to Qiantang and was confined in a separate residence.
translations.idiomatic: At Renquan's arrival Yuanxiang trembled with fear; he returned to Qiantang and was confined in a separate residence.

sentences.zh: 仁詮，湖州人也。

translations.literal: Renquan was a native of Hu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Renquan was from Hu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 閩主改福州為長樂府。

translations.literal: The Min ruler changed Fuzhou Prefecture to Changle Prefecture-fu.
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler renamed Fuzhou Prefecture as Changle Prefecture-fu.

sentences.zh: 親從都指揮使王仁達有擒王延稟之功，性慷慨，言事無所避。

translations.literal: Personal guard overall commander Wang Renda had the achievement of capturing Wang Yanbin; his nature was generous and forthright, and in speaking of affairs he avoided nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Personal guard overall commander Wang Renda had captured Wang Yanbin; generous and forthright by nature, he spoke his mind without reservation.

sentences.zh: 閩主惡之，嘗私謂左右曰：「仁達智有餘，吾猶能御之，非少主臣也。」

translations.literal: The Min ruler hated him and once said privately to his attendants, "Renda has more than enough wit — I can still control him, but he is no minister for a young ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler hated him and once told his attendants privately, "Renda has wit to spare — I can still control him, but he is no minister for a young ruler.

sentences.zh: 至是，竟誣以叛，族誅之。

translations.literal: At this time he was ultimately framed for rebellion and his whole clan executed.
translations.idiomatic: Now he was framed for rebellion and his entire clan executed.

sentences.zh: 初，馬希聲、希範同日生。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ma Xisheng and Xifan were born on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xisheng and Xifan had been born on the same day.

sentences.zh: 希聲母曰袁德妃，希範母曰陳氏。

translations.literal: Xisheng's mother was Consort Yuan De; Xifan's mother was the Chen clan.
translations.idiomatic: Xisheng's mother was Consort Yuan De; Xifan's mother was Lady Chen.

sentences.zh: 希範怨希聲先立不止，及嗣位，不禮於袁德妃。

translations.literal: Xifan resented that Xisheng had been made heir apparent first and would not desist; once he succeeded to the throne, he showed no courtesy to Consort Yuan De.
translations.idiomatic: Xifan resented that Xisheng had been made heir first and would not yield; once enthroned, he showed no courtesy to Consort Yuan De.

sentences.zh: 希聲母弟希旺為親從都指揮使，希範多譴責之。

translations.literal: Xisheng's younger brother by the same mother, Xiwang, was personal guard overall commander; Xifan frequently reprimanded and blamed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xisheng's maternal younger brother Xiwang served as personal guard overall commander; Xifan frequently rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 袁德妃請納希旦官為道士，不許，解其軍職，使居竹屋草門，不得預兄弟燕集。

translations.literal: Consort Yuan De asked to have Xidan's official post taken as a Daoist priest; this was not permitted — his military post was removed, he was made to dwell in a bamboo house with a grass gate, and was not allowed to join his brothers' feasts.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yuan De asked that Xidan be made a Daoist priest — denied. His military post was stripped, he was made to live in a bamboo hut with a grass gate, and barred from his brothers' gatherings.

sentences.zh: 德妃卒，希旦憂憤而卒。

translations.literal: Consort De died; Xidan died of grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: When Consort De died, Xidan died of grief and anger.

sentences.zh: 潞王上

translations.literal: Prince of Lu, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Lu, Part One

sentences.zh: 明宗聖德和武欽孝皇帝下清泰元年（

translations.literal: Below: Emperor Mingzong, Sagely Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Reverently Filial — the first year of Qingtai (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang — first year of the Qingtai era (

sentences.zh: 甲午，公元九三四年）

translations.literal: jiawu, AD 934)
translations.idiomatic: jiawu, AD 934)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊寅，閔帝大赦，改元應順。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on wuyin, Emperor Min granted a general amnesty and changed the era name to Yingshun.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on wuyin, Emperor Min proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Yingshun.

sentences.zh: 壬午，加河陽節度使兼侍衛都指揮使康義誠兼侍中，判六軍諸衛事。

translations.literal: On renwu, Heyang governor and Palace Guard overall commander Kang Yicheng was additionally made Palace Attendant and put in charge of the Six Armies and various guard units.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Heyang governor and Palace Guard overall commander Kang Yicheng was made Palace Attendant as well and put in charge of the Six Armies and all guard units.

sentences.zh: 朱弘昭、馮贇忌侍衛馬軍都指揮使、寧國節度使安彥威、侍衛步軍都指揮使、忠正節度使張從賓，甲申，出彥威為護國節度使，以捧聖馬軍都指揮使朱洪實代之；

translations.literal: Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun envied Palace Guard horse army commander and Ningguo governor An Yanwei and Palace Guard foot army commander and Zhongzheng governor Zhang Congbin; on jiashen, Yanwei was sent out as Huguo governor, and Sacred Guard horse army commander Zhu Hongshi replaced him;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun envied Palace Guard horse commander and Ningguo governor An Yanwei and Palace Guard foot commander and Zhongzheng governor Zhang Congbin. On jiashen, Yanwei was sent out as Huguo governor, with Sacred Guard horse commander Zhu Hongshi replacing him;

sentences.zh: 出從賓為彰義節度使，以嚴衛步軍都指揮使皇甫遇代之。

translations.literal: Congbin was sent out as Zhangyi governor, and Strict Guard foot army commander Huangfu Yu replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Congbin was sent out as Zhangyi governor, with Strict Guard foot commander Huangfu Yu replacing him.

sentences.zh: 彥威，崞人；

translations.literal: Yanwei was a man of Guo;
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei was from Guo;

sentences.zh: 遇，真定人也。

translations.literal: Yu was a native of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was from Zhending.

sentences.zh: 戊子，樞密使、同平章事朱弘昭、同中書門下二品馮贇、河東節度使兼侍中石敬瑭並兼中書令。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Bureau Commissioner and Associate Grand Councilor Zhu Hongzhao, Second Rank of the Secretariat and Chancellery Feng Yun, and Hedong governor and Palace Attendant Shi Jingtang were all additionally made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Bureau Commissioner and Associate Grand Councilor Zhu Hongzhao, Second Rank under the Secretariat and Chancellery Feng Yun, and Hedong governor and Palace Attendant Shi Jingtang were all made Director of the Secretariat as well.

sentences.zh: 贇以超遷太過，堅辭不受；

translations.literal: Yun, saying the promotion was too great a leap, firmly declined and would not accept;
translations.idiomatic: Yun said the promotion was too sudden and firmly declined;

sentences.zh: 己丑，改兼侍中。

translations.literal: On jichou, he was changed to additional Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, he was instead made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以荊南節度使高從誨為南平王，武安、武平節度使馬希範為楚王。

translations.literal: On renchen, Jingnan governor Gao Conghui was made Prince of Nanping, and Wu'an and Wuping governor Ma Xifan was made Prince of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Jingnan governor Gao Conghui was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanping, and Wu'an and Wuping governor Ma Xifan as Prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以鎮海、鎮東節度使吳王元瓘為吳越王。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Zhenhai and Zhendong governor King of Wu Yuanqian was made King of Wuyue.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Zhenhai and Zhendong governor King of Wu Yuanqian was enfeoffed as King of Wuyue.

sentences.zh: 吳徐知誥別治私第於金陵，乙未，遷居私第，虛府捨以待吳主。

translations.literal: Xu Zhigao of Wu separately built a private residence at Jinling; on yiwei, he moved to the private residence, leaving the official residence empty to await the Wu ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhigao of Wu had built a private residence at Jinling; on yiwei he moved into it, leaving the official residence empty for the Wu ruler.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔節度使兼侍中潞王從珂，與石敬瑭少從明帝征伐，有功名，得眾心。

translations.literal: Fengxiang governor and Palace Attendant Prince of Lu Congke, with Shi Jingtang, had from youth followed Emperor Ming in campaigns; they had merit and fame and won the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang governor and Palace Attendant Prince of Lu Congke had campaigned at Emperor Ming's side from youth with Shi Jingtang; both had merit, fame, and the soldiers' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 朱弘昭、馮贇位望素出二人下遠甚，一旦執朝政，皆忌之。

translations.literal: Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun's rank and prestige had always been far below the two men; once they seized court governance, they envied them both.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun had always ranked far below the two men; now that they held power, they envied them both.

sentences.zh: 明宗有疾，潞王屢遣其夫人入省侍；

translations.literal: When Mingzong fell ill, the Prince of Lu repeatedly sent his lady in to visit and attend him;
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong fell ill, the Prince of Lu repeatedly sent his wife to the palace to attend him;

sentences.zh: 及明宗殂，潞王辭疾不來，使臣至鳳翔者或自言伺得潞王陰事。

translations.literal: When Mingzong died, the Prince of Lu pleaded illness and did not come; envoys reaching Fengxiang sometimes claimed of their own accord to have spied out the Prince of Lu's secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong died, the Prince of Lu pleaded illness and stayed away; some envoys who reached Fengxiang claimed to have uncovered his secret dealings.

sentences.zh: 時潞王長子重吉為控鶴都指揮使，朱、馮不欲其典禁兵，己亥，出為亳州團練使。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Lu's eldest son Chongji was Control Cranes commander; Zhu and Feng did not want him commanding the forbidden troops; on jihai, he was sent out as Boz Prefecture training commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu's eldest son Chongji then commanded the Control Cranes; Zhu and Feng did not want him holding the forbidden troops — on jihai he was sent out as training commissioner of Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 潞王有女惠明為尼，在洛陽，亦召入禁中。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu had a daughter Huiming who was a nun in Luoyang; she too was summoned into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu had a daughter, Huiming, a nun in Luoyang — she too was summoned into the palace.

sentences.zh: 潞王由是疑懼。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu from this grew suspicious and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Lu grew suspicious and afraid.

sentences.zh: 吳蔣延徽敗閩兵於浦城，遂圍建州，閩主璘遣上軍張彥柔、驃騎大將軍王延宗將兵萬人救建州。

translations.literal: Jiang Yanhui of Wu defeated Min troops at Pucheng and then besieged Jian Prefecture; Min ruler Lin sent Chief of Staff Zhang Yanrou and Flying Cavalry Grand General Wang Yanzong to lead ten thousand troops to rescue Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yanhui of Wu defeated Min troops at Pucheng and besieged Jian Prefecture; Min ruler Lin sent Chief of Staff Zhang Yanrou and Flying Cavalry Grand General Wang Yanzong with ten thousand men to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 延宗軍及中塗，士卒不進，曰：「不得薛文傑，不能討賊。」

translations.literal: Yanzong's army had reached halfway when the soldiers would not advance, saying, "Without getting Xue Wenjie, we cannot punish the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong's army had marched halfway when the troops refused to advance, crying, "Without Xue Wenjie we cannot punish the enemy!

sentences.zh: 延宗馳使以聞，國人震恐。

translations.literal: Yanzong sent a fast messenger to report this; the people of the state were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzong sent a fast messenger to report it — the nation was shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 太后及福王繼鵬泣謂璘曰：「文傑盜弄國權，枉害無辜，上下怨怒久矣。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager and Prince of Fu Jipeng wept and said to Lin, "Wenjie usurped and wielded state power, wrongfully harmed the innocent — resentment above and below has been long.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager and Prince of Fu Jipeng wept and told Lin, "Wenjie has usurped state power and wrongfully harmed the innocent — court and people have hated him for years.

sentences.zh: 今吳兵深入，士卒不進，社稷一旦傾覆，留文傑何益！」

translations.literal: Now Wu troops have penetrated deep; the soldiers will not advance — the altars of state may fall in a day; what good is keeping Wenjie!
translations.idiomatic: Wu troops have penetrated deep, the soldiers refuse to advance — the state may fall in a day. What good is keeping Wenjie!"

sentences.zh: 文傑亦在側，互陳利害。

translations.literal: Wenjie was also at the side; each stated advantages and harms.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjie was present as well; each side argued the stakes.

sentences.zh: 璘曰：「吾無如卿何，卿自為謀。」

translations.literal: Lin said, "I can do nothing with you — devise your own plan.
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "There is nothing I can do for you — look to your own salvation.

sentences.zh: 文傑出，繼鵬伺之於啟聖門外，以笏擊之仆地，檻車送軍前，市人爭持瓦礫擊之。

translations.literal: Wenjie went out; Jipeng waited for him outside the Qisheng Gate, struck him with a tablet until he fell to the ground, sent him in a prisoner cart to the army front, and market people vied to pelt him with tiles and stones.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjie left; Jipeng waited outside the Qisheng Gate, struck him down with a court tablet, and sent him to the army in a prisoner cart — townspeople vied to pelt him with rubble.

sentences.zh: 文傑善術數，自雲過三日則無患。

translations.literal: Wenjie was skilled in numerology and arts; he said himself that after three days passed there would be no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjie practiced divination and declared that after three days he would be safe.

sentences.zh: 部送者聞之，倍道兼行，二日而至，士卒見之踴躍，臠食之；

translations.literal: Those escorting him, hearing this, traveled double marches on combined roads; in two days they arrived; the soldiers upon seeing him leaped for joy and dismembered and ate him;
translations.idiomatic: His escorts, hearing this, forced double marches and arrived in two days — the soldiers leaped for joy at the sight and tore him to pieces;

sentences.zh: 閩主亟遣赦之，不及。

translations.literal: The Min ruler hastily sent orders to pardon him — too late.
translations.idiomatic: The Min ruler hastily sent a pardon — too late.

sentences.zh: 初，文傑以為古制檻車疏闊，更為之，形如木匱，攢以鐵鋩，內向，動輒觸之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wenjie thought the prisoner cart of ancient regulation was too loose and made a new one shaped like a wooden chest, studded with iron spikes turned inward — at every movement one struck them.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjie had found the old-style prisoner cart too roomy and designed a new one shaped like a wooden chest, studded with inward-pointing iron spikes — the slightest movement drew blood.

sentences.zh: 車成，文傑首自入焉。

translations.literal: When the cart was finished, Wenjie was the first to enter it himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the cart was finished, Wenjie was the first to enter it.

sentences.zh: 並誅盛韜。

translations.literal: Sheng Tao was also executed.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Tao was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 蔣延徽攻建州垂克，徐知誥以延徽吳太祖之婿，與臨川王濛素善，恐其克建州奉濛以圖興復，遣使召之。

translations.literal: Jiang Yanhui's attack on Jian Prefecture was nearly successful; Xu Zhigao, because Yanhui was son-in-law to Wu's founding emperor and was on good terms with Prince of Linchuan Meng, feared that if he took Jian Prefecture he would install Meng to plot restoration — he sent envoys to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yanhui was on the verge of taking Jian Prefecture when Xu Zhigao, knowing Yanhui was the Wu founder's son-in-law and close to Prince of Linchuan Meng, feared that capturing the city would let Meng mount a restoration — and summoned him back.

sentences.zh: 延徽亦聞閩兵及吳越兵將至，引兵歸；

translations.literal: Yanhui also heard that Min troops and Wuyue troops were about to arrive and withdrew his army;
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui also heard that Min and Wuyue troops were approaching and withdrew;

sentences.zh: 閩人追擊，敗之，士卒死亡甚眾，歸罪於都虞侯張重進，斬之。

translations.literal: Min people pursued and struck, defeating him; soldiers died in great numbers; blame was assigned to Chief Adjutant Zhang Chongjin, who was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Min forces pursued and routed him with heavy losses; blame fell on Chief Adjutant Zhang Chongjin, who was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 知誥貶延徽為右威衛將軍，遣使求好於閩。

translations.literal: Zhigao demoted Yanhui to Right Prestige Guard general and sent envoys seeking goodwill with Min.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao demoted Yanhui to Right Prestige Guard general and sent envoys seeking peace with Min.

sentences.zh: 閏月，以左諫議大夫唐汭、膳部郎中、知制誥陳乂皆為給事中，充樞密直學士。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Left Remonstrance Grandee Tang Rui and Board of Provisions Director and Drafting Commissioner Chen Yi were both made Supervising Secretaries and appointed Direct Secretarial Academicians of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Left Remonstrance Grandee Tang Rui and Board of Provisions Director and Drafting Commissioner Chen Yi were both made Supervising Secretaries and Direct Secretarial Academicians of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 汭以文學從帝，歷三鎮在幕府。

translations.literal: Rui for his literary talent had followed the emperor and served in three circuits' headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Rui had followed the emperor for his literary talent, serving in three circuits' headquarters.

sentences.zh: 及即位，將佐之有才者，朱、馮皆斥逐之。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne, capable generals and staff — Zhu and Feng drove them all away.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Zhu and Feng drove away every capable general and aide.

sentences.zh: 汭性過疏，朱、馮恐帝含怒有時而發，乃引汭於密近，以其黨陳乂監之。

translations.literal: Rui's nature was overly loose; Zhu and Feng feared the emperor's hidden anger might erupt in time, and therefore drew Rui close in confidential service, using their partisan Chen Yi to watch him.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was too undisciplined by nature; Zhu and Feng feared the emperor's smoldering anger might one day erupt, and so kept Rui close — with their ally Chen Yi set to watch him.

sentences.zh: 丙午，尊皇后為皇太后。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the empress was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the empress was honored as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 安遠節度使符彥超奴王希全、任駕兒見朝廷多事，謀殺彥超，據安州附於吳，夜，叩門稱有急遞，彥超出至聽事，二奴殺之，因以彥超之命召諸將，有不從己者輒殺之。

translations.literal: Anyuan governor Fu Yanchao's slaves Wang Xiquan and Ren Jia'er, seeing that the court had many troubles, plotted to kill Yanchao, hold An Prefecture, and submit to Wu; at night they knocked at the gate claiming an urgent dispatch; Yanchao came out to the reception hall and the two slaves killed him; then in Yanchao's name they summoned the generals — whoever would not follow them was immediately killed.
translations.idiomatic: Anyuan governor Fu Yanchao's slaves Wang Xiquan and Ren Jia'er, seeing turmoil at court, plotted to kill Yanchao, seize An Prefecture, and submit to Wu. At night they knocked at the gate claiming an urgent dispatch; when Yanchao came to headquarters the two slaves killed him, then summoned the generals in his name — any who refused were killed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 己酉旦，副使李端帥州兵討誅之，並其黨。

translations.literal: At dawn on jiyou, Deputy Commissioner Li Duan led prefectural troops to campaign against and execute them, along with their faction.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on jiyou, Deputy Commissioner Li Duan led prefectural troops against them and executed them along with their followers.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以王淑妃為太妃。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Consort Wang Shufei was made Senior Consort.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Consort Wang Shufei was elevated to Senior Consort.

sentences.zh: 蜀將吏勸蜀王知祥稱帝。

translations.literal: Shu's generals and officials urged King of Shu Zhixiang to declare himself emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's generals and officials urged King of Shu Zhixiang to take the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 己巳，知祥即皇帝位於成都。

translations.literal: On jisi, Zhixiang took the imperial throne at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Zhixiang declared himself emperor at Chengdu.
